articles.title: Fantasy Football: What happened to the tight end position this season? Scott Pianowski investigates
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski examines the state of the tight end position in 2026.
articles.body:
I'm spending my mid-November the way most good fantasy football managers are. I'm doing roster audits, schedule surveying and trying to figure out who's in the Circle of Trust and who's not. We wanted to get off to a fast start, we wanted to control October, we wanted to get into position to get into position. Check, check, check. Now let's bring this thing home.

And as I went through my checkpoints this week, a sneaky theme begged for my attention. What the heck happened at tight end? When did this position get so gross ?

Isaiah Likely (TE11 in draft season, TE2 thus far) has been the position's biggest hit, and George Kittle (TE9/TE4) has shown that basic rehab rules don't apply to him. See you in the Hall of Fame, 85.

But what's causing so much agita elsewhere? Let's investigate.

For the most part, it's been smooth sailing for the vanity tight ends. Bowers has been a little dinged up, missed two games. He might not be healthy the remainder of the year. But he's shown the ability to produce in any kind of environment. McBride has long shown his ability to command targets, and the Cardinals routinely face negative game script — good for garbage-time production.

Alas, the Raiders and Cardinals have both rebooted at the QB position. Kirk Cousins was surprisingly sharp for nine games and the Raiders decided to flip the asset and bank the profit, shipping him to QB-needy Minnesota. The Cardinals did a similar thing to a lesser degree, moving Jacoby Brissett to desperate Baltimore after the Ravens lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Sure, Brissett was already benched in Arizona, replaced by Gardner Minshew. But Minshew wound up getting hurt in his first start.

Bowers and McBride now have to make things work with unproven rookies Fernando Mendoza and Carson Beck. Obviously, the ceilings are different for these freshmen — Mendoza won the Heisman Trophy last year and was the first overall pick in the draft, while Beck was merely the 65th pick in the same class. But neither player looked ready last week, albeit the assignments were stark — Mendoza faced the Seahawks, Beck drew the Rams.

Bottom line with Bowers and McBride, we usually bet on talent in these spots. They've produced with lesser QBs before, and Mendoza and Beck will likely improve as they gain more reps. But you can't blame anyone who's pining for good old days, like September 2026, when the Raiders and Cardinals had experience in the QB chair.

It's easy to forget, but for about 10 weeks last year, the Colts had an elite offense. They were sitting at 8-2 after an overtime win over the Falcons, racking up 519 yards of offense. The AFC South was there for the taking.

And nothing has gone right since. Close losses to Kansas City and Houston followed after a bye week, and then Daniel Jones got hurt. Indianapolis finished the year on a seven-game losing streak and didn't make the playoffs.

Just about everything has crapped out here in 2026. Alec Pierce received a big extension but he's hardly played, hounded by injury. He's likely done for the year. Jones' return from his torn Achilles tendon has been a mess — league-high 12 picks, lousy 67.0 rating, just 183 yards per game. Jonathan Taylor has been credible but he's down to 4.2 YPC, the worst average of his seven-year career.

This is a roundabout way of saying Warren's frustration-filled second year isn't really his fault. Warren's also had his own injury concerns, missing two games with a groin pull. Desperate fantasy managers are wondering if forgotten backup QB Anthony Richardson Sr. might be an improvement as the Colts start scouting for the future.

Although Pitts' disappointing year is obviously tied to Atlanta's mediocre QB room, Pitts also has to own some of his disappointing metrics. He's down to 9.3 YPC and he doesn't command targets, averaging fewer than five per game. A little touchdown deodorant (four spikes) has slightly cushioned the blow, but Pitts has zero floor in any week. You need a better option if you want to have a legitimate playoff chance.

Loveland was being fitted for Bust of the Year horns after a horrible opening two weeks (one piddly catch, three yards), and the Caleb Williams injury at the end of Week 2 also muddied the story. But since Williams returned, Loveland has joined the party: TE4, TE3, TE14, TE15. And those solid returns have come despite some pesky drops.

The Bears have a lovely schedule moving forward, and Loveland is ostensibly needed more with Cole Kmet out for the season. Loveland might never fully justify his summer helium, but he's a trustworthy candidate as we start making playoff plans.

Kraft was having a glorious breakout year in 2025 before tearing his ACL in Week 9. But the draft market couldn't help itself all summer, pointing to Kraft's splashy metrics and figuring that even if he started the year less than 100%, he'd get there eventually.

Kraft hasn't been a bust — just landing anyone who's inside the starting line at tight end feels like a win this year. But his YPC is down over five yards, and his yards per target has dropped from 11.1 to 6.6. The Green Bay offense has been forced to rely on the pass most of the year as the run blocking has struggled, and Kraft has been pressed into more blocking assignments than fantasy managers would like. But it's also tough to watch Jordan Love, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden all have breakout years while Kraft is left in the station.

I'm ready to draft Kraft proactively next year, a full season removed from the ACL blowout. But we likely have to keep expectations modest for the rest of 2026, as unsatisfying a conclusion as that might be.

These guys are basically returning their ADPs, and sometimes a par is what you need. But the upside is always capped with Fannin and LaPorta because of how talented their teammates are. Cleveland landed two impactful wideouts in the draft, instant-ready talents, and LaPorta will always be fighting Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams for opportunities. It will be interesting to see if the Lions and LaPorta can figure out a contract extension; negotiations have been somewhat acrimonious, and for now, they've broken off.

In mid-September, it looked like Kincaid was a screaming right answer. He had 130 yards at Houston in the opener, then gashed Detroit with a 7-95-1 line. Finally healthy and ready for an increased snap share, we got ready for the moon.

Physical attrition has taken over since then — a rib injury, a sprained ankle. Kincaid hasn't missed any time, but he's seen more than three targets in just one of his last seven games. If you sort through tight end stats starting in Week 3, Kincaid falls to TE24.

Part of this is life with Josh Allen, a superstar who hasn't peppered any teammate with targets since Stefon Diggs left. Consider that in Allen's MVP season two years ago, Mack Hollins' five touchdowns were the most on the team. Injuries are part of the 2026 story in Buffalo, but no one has more than 45 targets or three touchdown catches. Allen and James Cook III are the stat hogs on this Super Bowl contender; everyone else is something of a fringe play.

Age and natural attrition have kept Travis Kelce on the TE1/2 seam, good enough to roster but never an automatic start.

The Rams always have a slew of interesting tight ends, but even with cluster injuries at WR, none of the tight ends have scored consistently. Terrance Ferguson has had trouble staying healthy.

Pat Freiermuth always feels like a preferred streamer, but Aaron Rodgers has started to look his age over the last month.

If T.J. Hockenson can get healthy, maybe Kirk Cousins can cook up some PPR scam down the stretch.

Brenton Strange is never going to be a target hog in Jacksonville, but at least his efficiency metrics are good. The Jaguars have a favorable schedule moving forward.

Mike Gesicki is never a volume bet, but at least he offers touchdown equity on one of the NFL's most bankable passing games.

articles.title: 49ers, Vikings Take Opposite Approaches To Preparing For Mexico City Altitude
articles.summary: The NFL returns to Mexico City on Sunday, and the Vikings and 49ers have taken very different routes to the same 7,000-plus feet of altitude.
articles.body: The NFL returns to Mexico City on Sunday, and the Vikings and 49ers have taken very different routes to the same 7,000-plus feet of altitude. The two teams are set to meet at Estadio Banorte, formerly known as Estadio Azteca, in the NFL’s first game in Mexico City since 2022. The stadium sits roughly 7,352 feet above sea level, more than 2,000 feet higher than Denver. The 49ers hold the top seed in the NFC after a 46-40 win over the Cowboys. The Vikings are coming off a 30-10 win at Green Bay that snapped a two-game losing streak. It’s Minnesota’s first game in Mexico. San Francisco flew from Dallas to Colorado Springs after beating the Cowboys and is spending the week practicing at the Air Force Academy before flying to Mexico City on Saturday. Minnesota is staying home, with a plan built around a high-altitude room at its facility and a quick trip: the Vikings fly in Saturday and leave right after the game. Vikings vice president of health and performance Tyler Williams said the plan has been in place for weeks. "I'd say to date, we have close to 450 sessions accumulated in there. Nearly our whole roster has done five-plus sessions and nearly our whole roster has [experienced] 12,000 feet, which is great," Williams said. Williams added that preserving routine was a big part of the reasoning for staying at home. "Players love that Sunday-to-Sunday weekly rhythm," Williams said. Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said the preparation began "weeks ago" and that the staff talked to soccer teams, NBA teams and others who deal with the same challenges. O’Connell said the offense plans to rotate players where it can, noting that a lot of it will happen naturally through personnel changes. "We’re going to have to just navigate the types of things that maybe we would normally be a little bit more aggressive with, or maybe it’s using tempo, and then backing off and making sure we’re within the confines of the play clock, our substitutions," O’Connell said. "We’re going to go compete for 60 minutes, whatever it takes." Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores said the defense will need to rotate, too, saying "everybody’s going to have to be ready to play." 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he doesn’t think altitude decides games, but he acknowledged it helps to be acclimated. "I always think the Broncos have a 2% advantage every time at home because they’re just more used to it. But 2% doesn’t win you games," Shanahan said. "It’s definitely nicer to play in something when you’re acclimated to that altitude, so you’re not as out of breath. But it’s rarely the difference in winning and losing. But anything that helps, if it works for a team, we try to do it." The 49ers have been to Mexico City before. They beat the Arizona Cardinals 38-10 there in 2022, and Shanahan said it felt like a home game. "I always joke, I go to Cabo a lot. I feel like our Mexican fan base is off the chain," Shanahan told reporters. "They’re unbelievable. They could come up to wherever we go, and definitely expecting to be there in Mexico City." 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey said he’s looking forward to going back. "It was one of the coolest experiences playing there. That many people being that loud for that long was something that was really special," McCaffrey said. "All the Mexican fans are unbelievable, so we can’t wait to get down there." The 49ers last trip south of the border wasn’t all smooth. Shanahan said the last bus of players, which usually arrives about three hours before kickoff, got lost on the way to the stadium and arrived an hour and 15 minutes before the game with about 12 starters on board. Beyond the delayed arrival and a delayed exit due to customs, he had nothing but praise for the experience. "The stadium was awesome. The atmosphere was great," Shanahan said. "It was a really cool place to play football." FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Updated Ranking for NHL Winter Classic Jerseys After Mammoth and Avalanche Reveal
articles.summary: The 2027 Winter Classic is coming soon and the matchup between the Colorado Avalanche and Utah Mammoth at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on December 31 provides a great setting for an outdoor game. What makes the Winter Classic even better? The uniforms the teams wear for the game.
articles.body:
The 2027 Winter Classic is coming soon and the matchup between the Colorado Avalanche and Utah Mammoth at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on December 31 provides a great setting for an outdoor game. What makes the Winter Classic even better? The uniforms the teams wear for the game.

Both Colorado and Utah unveiled what they'll be wearing for the game and aside from crushing it with the designs, it got us thinking about where these new jerseys stack up all-time. After all, the Winter Classic has been around since 2008 so we've got a lot of looks to compare and contrast against each other and the Avalanche and Mammoth very well may have the best we've seen in some time.

But where do they fall in line compared to what we've seen over the years? Let's hash it out and pick out the 10 best jerseys since the inception of the Winter Classic. There's no science to this other than fashion, beauty, and classic style creating the best looks possible so let's get to it.

The 2025 Winter Classic may not have gone the way the Chicago Blackhawks wanted it to go, losing to the St. Louis Blues at Wrigley Field, but after appearing in the annual event multiple times, they absolutely nailed it with their jerseys for this game.

Chicago kept the classic red jersey with the white and black stripes, as well as their legendary iconography, done with a twist on the front with a circular-style logo with the team's name in it. It's very much like Chicago's regular home jersey but very much different given the logo tweaks.

It's a great-looking sweater and fits in well with everything the franchise has had over its many years in existence. Part of the fun of the Winter Classic is having a uniform that either was from the past or looks like something that belongs to the old days, and this one hit all those notes perfectly.

The Bruins have been part of many Winter Classic matchups, and they've had consistently great jerseys for all of them. The look they went for in the 2023 game against the Pittsburgh Penguins at Fenway Park, however, made use of a secondary Bruins logo that's beloved all the same.

The classically cartoonish snarling Bruin that adorned the shoulders of their jerseys in the 80s and early 90s got prime positioning on the front for the 2023 game. With "BOSTON" spelled out over it and the black and gold colors, there was no mistaking who the Penguins were facing off against.

The "meth bear" crest with the black and gold stripes on the sleeves made this jersey a fashionable hit, although the Bruins' many appearances in the Winter Classic may have stolen thunder away from how great these jerseys were.

The Montréal Canadiens became the second Canadian team to appear in the Winter Classic in 2016 when they went to Gillette Stadium in Foxboro, Massachusetts, to take on the Boston Bruins. To celebrate facing their ancient rivals, they dusted off an old look and made it new.

The Canadiens jersey is styled after their 1924-1925 home jerseys but with a couple of switches. For one, this jersey is white as opposed to red, and secondly, the globe that appears on the sleeve was on the front of the 24-25 jerseys instead, with the legendary "CH" logo on the sleeves. Paying homage to the past and making it something new is the kind of catnip we love for these events.

Having a white jersey with a lighter blue color and red highlights helped them stand out more against the Bruins' darker colors, but for the Habs to do something similar but different to their already perfect jerseys and make it work? That's the good stuff.

What we know about the Penguins' Winter Classic jerseys from 2011, when they hosted at Heinz Field against the rival Washington Capitals, is that their homage to the early days of the team never looked better. What we found out later was that fans ended up viewing this spectacular jersey as cursed.

The Penguins used inspiration from the team's early years in the 60s and 70s for this design, and with the dark and light blue colors, it's really hard to look at this jersey and think it's at all bad. The circular logo with the skating penguin with its scarf blowing in the breeze is also a throwback, and yet the whole of this design was new.

However, the Pens lost to the Capitals 3-1, and Sidney Crosby took a wicked hit from Dave Steckel in the game that contributed to concussion issues that season, and the Penguins ultimately didn't go as far as fans hoped, thus damning the jerseys as cursed. If these threads are bad news, then we can't get enough of them. They're outstanding.

The Colorado Avalanche have been part of the Stadium Series but never a Winter Classic, and their debut in the event this season shows that maybe we should've seen them sooner if they were going to look this good.

The Avs jerseys for the 2027 Winter Classic are immediate hits. The white sweater with the dark blue shoulders and sleeve stripes also has a white stripe within the shoulders that makes it something entirely unique. The crest is brand new, with a stylized "C" with the mountains embedded in the empty space of the letter, and the jersey itself has notches and designs debossed within the letter and mountains to give it sneaky additional design.

It's a clean-looking jersey, and the whole of it is gorgeous. This one, along with what Host Utah is wearing, helps set the bar high for future Winter Classic jerseys.

When the Bruins hosted and took part in their first Winter Classic in 2010 against the Philadelphia Flyers at Fenway Park, they showed up knocking it out of the park in throwback-inspired gold jerseys that really upped the ante for future participants.

The Bruins' gold sweaters used a spoked-B logo the team used back in 1948-49, and the gold and dusty black/maybe brown color scheme gave it its own old-fashioned feel.

Skating out on the ice in these uniforms against the Flyers with a classic look of their own gave this game the kind of throwback feel unique to the event. In this case, it was like seeing an old Bruins team going up against the Broad Street Bullies, until Marco Sturm scored the winning goal to send the Bruins faithful at Fenway home happy, and the players never looked better than they did at this Winter Classic in Boston.

In 2024, the Seattle Kraken and Vegas Golden Knights, the league's two newest franchises, made their Winter Classic debuts, and while we liked what Vegas wore for the game, the Kraken owned the day at T-Mobile Park in Seattle.

The Kraken's jerseys were inspired by the Seattle Metropolitans, the Stanley Cup Champions of 1914, with horizontal stripes throughout the jersey. The Kraken "S" logo adorned the front in salmon red, and rather than spelling out "SEATTLE" as the Metropolitans jersey did back in the day, this one spelled out "KRAKEN" within the "S."

As far as homage jerseys go, this one is spot-on, and with the Kraken's color scheme setting the palette for it, it absolutely crushed the look. Even though it's a very close comparison to the old Metropolitan jerseys, this one is just different enough to keep us happy.

The 2014 Winter Classic may have been the most picturesque of all the outdoor games. From the setting at Michigan Stadium and the cold, snowy weather to the uniforms worn by both teams, it was the perfect overall aesthetic. It was also the rare Winter Classic (at that time) where both teams nailed the look.

For the Maple Leafs, the first Canadian team to play in a Winter Classic, they brought it hard for their jerseys. The blue and white stripes, the old-time-style Maple Leafs logo that throws it back to their original logo from the 1920s, and the overall classic style of the jersey itself made it a perfect jersey for the event.

What also helped make it look good was how the Leafs upended the host Red Wings in a shootout in a snowstorm with over 100,000 fans in attendance.

As good as the Maple Leafs looked in the 2014 Winter Classic, the host Detroit Red Wings made it look even better.

Donned in red jerseys to counter the Maple Leafs' blue sweaters, it provided the first all-color matchup, but Detroit made their look sing with an old-time-styled winged wheel as well as spelling out "DETROIT" above it. With the cream-white colors, it gave it an old-school look, as well as the unique captain patches that appeared on the sleeves as opposed to the body of the jersey; everything about this jersey says it's a throwback, except that it was entirely new.

Detroit and Toronto crushed it with the 2014 game, but the Red Wings made sure to do a little bit more with their look to make home fans that much happier.

For years we've gone to the mat for the 2014 Winter Classic jersey matchup between Detroit and Toronto as the best jerseys we've seen, but that day is over. The Utah Mammoth own the crown now.

When Utah introduced baby sky blue as a color for their team, we've been waiting for a killer alternate using it for a jersey. Their Hometown Remix does that , and while that's fine, their jersey for the 2027 Winter Classic blows it out of the water. It's got the old-timey style to it with the stripes, but it's also got a full-sized mammoth as part of the crest, and we've never wanted anything more.

Having "UTAH" in text is nice as are the shoulder logos, but everything about this jersey sings loud and proud. It's a magnificent look and we cannot wait to see it on the ice at the Winter Classic in Salt Lake City. We can only hope that it sticks around beyond this one game and for years to come.

articles.title: "We need real investment": Lewis Hamilton challenges Formula One to do more for underrepresented communities as Mission 44 celebrates five years
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton, the seven time Formula One World champion, remains pretty serious about his high profile romance with the billionaire SKIMS founder, Kim
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton, the seven time Formula One World champion, remains pretty serious about his high profile romance with the billionaire SKIMS founder, Kim Kardashian ever since they made their public debut during the Super Bowl in the last season. Amid this, Lewis Hamilton has called on F1, the FIA, and teams to accelerate diversity and inclusion efforts.Lewis Hamilton reflects on how the Formula One should expand their inclusion reports as his program continues to work for itA few hours ago, to celebrate the fifth anniversary of Mission 44 and the Hamilton Commission, according to The Guardian, Lewis Hamilton made a statement that read as, “Formula One is inspiring millions of young people around the world but inspiration means nothing without opportunity…We can’t tell young people to dream big and then not open the doors when they try to make those dreams a reality.”The seven time Formula One World champion added, “F1, the FIA and every team must push harder and move faster. We need real investment, more opportunities and greater accountability. We’ve shown that change is possible.”Lewis Hamilton continued, “Now we need to go further. The talent is out there, and the future of our sport depends on unlocking it…When I walk through the paddock now, I see more women, more Black and Brown faces, more people who look like the fans in the grandstands than at any point since I started. That is heartening, and the people behind it deserve credit. And yet, there is much still to do. We have opened the door, but we have not yet learned to count how many people walk through it…”What is Lewis Hamilton’s Mission 44 project all about and how he has helped people since its development?For the unversed, Lewis Hamilton’s Mission 44 focuses on inclusive education and STEM career opportunities to help young people from underrepresented and disadvantaged backgrounds thrive.Backed by £20 million of Lewis Hamilton's own funding and over £9 million awarded in grants, the charity has reached around 550,000 young people globally.According to reports, Lewis Hamilton’s Mission 44 frequently partners with groups like the Royal Academy of Engineering, AFBE-UK, and Driven By Us to fund Master's scholarships, worth up to £43,000 each, and mentorship for aspiring engineers.Several past scholars have moved into roles with F1 teams including Mercedes, Aston Martin, and Red Bull.But that’s not all; since 2022, Lewis Hamilton’s Mission 44 has funded Motorsport UK initiatives including Race for Diversity, Girls on Track Regional Hubs, and the Motorsport UK Inclusion Hub, reaching over 38,000 people and generating hundreds of training and employment opportunities.For now, the seven time Formula One World champion Lewis Hamilton remains focused on his career and inclusion efforts while his romance with Kim Kardashian has turned heads.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Actions speak louder than words”: Why Auston Matthews’ post-game comments could signal trouble for the Toronto Maple Leafs in the NHL
articles.summary: Auston Matthews expresses frustration over the Toronto Maple Leafs' inconsistent performance, raising concerns about the team's direction after a disappointing loss to the Chicago Blackhawks.
articles.body: Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews says he’s frustrated by the team’s inability to turn potential into consistent results following another disappointing loss. His post-game comments following the defeat against the Chicago Blackhawks have raised fresh questions about the team's direction and whether the organization can meet its ambitions.Matthews views the players and commitment in Toronto as a good team, but said the performance has to be up to the level of expectations. His statement, particularly the phrase "actions speak louder than words," has added to concerns surrounding the struggling NHL franchise.Auston Matthews questions Toronto Maple Leafs after Chicago Blackhawks lossAuston Matthews vented his frustration at the Toronto Maple Leafs’ performance after another loss, saying the team has to prove what it can do with results, not words. His comments have become another worrying development for a franchise struggling to find consistency during the 2026-27 NHL season."We can be a lot better team," Matthews said after the loss to the Chicago Blackhawks. However, he also made it clear that the difference between potential and actual performance remains a major concern."The most frustrating part is that I feel like we have what it takes to be a really good team," Matthews said. "We have a group that wants to compete every night and do the right things. But actions speak louder than words."Why are the Maple Leafs struggling to meet expectations?The franchise hoped roster changes, a new coaching staff and tweaks to its goaltending approach would help make Toronto more competitive early in the season.Instead, the Maple Leafs have been unable to find any rhythm and sit near the bottom of the Atlantic Division standings. Losing games against opponents such as the Chicago Blackhawks has added to the disappointment among supporters.Matthews remains one of the team’s most important players, and naturally he has high expectations. As captain, his comments also carry additional significance because they reflect concerns about the collective performance rather than an individual result.Could Auston Matthews' comments affect his Toronto future?Matthews’ comments have understandably raised questions about his future with the Toronto Maple Leafs long-term, especially considering the importance of winning championships in his career.The captain has long been linked with the expectation that Toronto should stay a legitimate contender. But his most recent comments are not confirmation that he wants out or that a trade is being considered.A potential deal would be a huge decision for the franchise. Matthews' value as an elite goal scorer could attract considerable interest from competing NHL teams, but losing its captain would also leave Toronto with a major leadership and offensive gap.For now, the immediate priority remains improving results. As pressure continues to build from supporters and the team’s direction is being examined more closely, the Maple Leafs need to demonstrate meaningful progress.Matthews’ message has made the challenge clear: Toronto needs to turn potential into performances before frustration becomes an even bigger concern.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: What has CM Punk revealed about his WWE future as rumors link him to a potential leadership position in NXT
articles.summary: CM Punk addresses retirement speculation, confirming his commitment to wrestling in WWE for at least five more years, amid rumors of a leadership role in NXT.
articles.body: CM Punk has quashed speculation that he's leaving pro wrestling for good to run NXT. Clearing up his future in WWE, the 48-year-old has confirmed he intends to remain an active in-ring competitor for at least another five years.His comments come amid reports of a possible WWE leadership reshuffle involving Shawn Michaels and Bruce Prichard, which have placed Punk's name in discussions about the future of the developmental brand.Why CM Punk is staying on WWE's active rosterCM Punk is not planning to give up his WWE wrestling career anytime soon, despite reports suggesting that he could eventually become involved in NXT leadership. During an NXT live event in Detroit on November 14, Punk directly addressed rumors about his future and confirmed his commitment to competing inside the ring.Punk teamed up with Bayley during the Detroit event, where the duo defeated Jackson Drake and Myka Lockwood in a mixed tag team match. Following their victory, both WWE stars addressed the audience, allowing Punk to respond to the growing speculation.According to reports from Fightful and Wrestling Observer, Punk acknowledged that some people believed his age meant he was preparing to end his wrestling career.But he dismissed that idea, saying to the audience:"Y'all stuck with me for at least five more years."Punk also reiterated his plans to continue wrestling at his current level until his body tells him to stop. His comments offered a direct indication that retirement is not part of his immediate plans.Why has CM Punk been linked to WWE NXT leadership?The speculation surrounding Punk began after PWInsider reported on November 13 that WWE was considering him as a potential successor to Shawn Michaels in overseeing NXT.The report suggested that Michaels could move into a larger creative position on WWE's main roster following expected changes involving Bruce Prichard after WrestleMania 43 in 2027.Currently Senior Vise President, Talent Development & Creative for WWE, Michaels has played an important role in developing NXT talent. If he moves into another position, WWE would need to consider who could take responsibility for the developmental brand.What does Dave Meltzer say about CM Punk's future role?Wrestling Observer's Dave Meltzer has also provided additional context about the possibility of Punk taking over NXT.Meltzer indicated that Punk would not immediately replace Michaels because he reportedly has five years remaining on a lucrative WWE contract. Moving into a full-time coaching or administrative position would mean giving up a significant part of his current in-ring career.For now, Punk remains focused on his active WWE career and upcoming competition. He is scheduled to represent Team USA against Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico in the traditional five-on-five elimination match at Survivor Series: WarGames.The upcoming Houston event allows Punk to continue to be involved in the big storylines in WWE rather than immediately going into a management role.His Detroit remarks also provide a key distinction between his long-term possibilities and immediate intentions. While WWE could consider him for a developmental leadership role in the future, Punk has made his current priority clear: continuing to wrestle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: James Rodríguez estrena un Lamborghini Revuelto en Medellín: el superdeportivo de más de $3.600 millones
articles.standfirst: La nueva adquisición de James se hizo viral en redes
articles.summary: La nueva adquisición de James se hizo viral en redes
articles.body: James Rodríguez volvió a colocarse en el centro de la conversación pública en Colombia no por un pase filtrado ni por una definición en el área, sino por una adquisición automotor de altísimo impacto en Medellín. El mediocampista cucuteño, referente de la Selección Colombia y figura de Atlético Nacional, apareció en redes sociales recibiendo las llaves de un Lamborghini Revuelto de color naranja brillante (Arancio Apodis), un superdeportivo híbrido enchufable cuya valoración comercial ronda los $3.670 millones de pesos colombianos. La noticia se viralizó tras la publicación de RR Autos (firma especializada vinculada a RRautos Diego), el concesionario antioqueño que gestionó la entrega del automóvil y acompañó el anuncio con un mensaje de felicitación etiquetando al futbolista. En cuestión de horas, el post acumuló decenas de miles de interacciones y encendió el debate entre aficionados, curiosos y seguidores del deporte sobre el diseño, la potencia y el millonario valor de este modelo en el mercado colombiano. El momento del estreno no pasó desapercibido en el entorno futbolístico del jugador. La divulgación de su nuevo vehículo ocurrió poco después de días de tensión deportiva tras quedar al margen de la final de la Copa BetPlay 2026, mientras el volante continúa sumando minutos y protagonismo con Atlético Nacional —con registros recientes que incluyen más de 800 minutos disputados, dos goles y tres asistencias en el campeonato. De acuerdo con reportes de medios y la divulgación del concesionario especializado, el ejemplar adquirido por James llevaba cerca de tres semanas disponible en vitrina antes de pasar a sus manos, convirtiéndose en una de las entregas de autos de alta gama más comentadas del año en Antioquia y en todo el país. Aunque el monto exacto pagado por el futbolista no fue revelado oficialmente, las referencias comerciales de la vitrina y del sector automotor de lujo ubican el valor de este Lamborghini Revuelto alrededor de los $3.670 millones de pesos. En el mercado colombiano, las estimaciones para una unidad de estas características suelen moverse en un rango amplio —entre $2.800 millones y $3.700 millones de pesos— dependiendo de factores clave como los impuestos y aranceles de importación, además de los paquetes de equipamiento y opciones de personalización. Más allá de su estética llamativa —con carrocería Arancio Apodis, contrastes en negro, rines deportivos, amplias tomas de aire laterales, luces LED de firma agresiva, las tradicionales puertas de tijera de la casa de Sant'Agata Bolognese y un habitáculo digital inspirado en la aviación—, el Revuelto representa la nueva generación de superdeportivos de la marca italiana. Como suele ocurrir cada vez que James Rodríguez comparte un aspecto de su vida privada o de su afición por los automóviles de alta gama, las reacciones se dividieron rápidamente entre los mensajes de felicitación de sus seguidores y los comentarios sobre el contraste entre el lujo extremo del superdeportivo y la coyuntura del fútbol local. Lo cierto es que el mediocampista volvió a captar los reflectores en Medellín, sumando una nueva pieza de colección a su historial automotor mientras sigue enfocado en su etapa con Atlético Nacional.

articles.title: New WWE Rumors on The Rock's Potential In-Ring Return Ahead of Survivor Series Appearance
articles.summary: WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson is reportedly not expected to return to the ring for a match in the near future despite this week's announcement that he will be in Houston for the Survivor Series premium live event on Nov. 28.
articles.body:
WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson is reportedly not expected to return to the ring for a match in the near future despite this week's announcement that he will be in Houston for the Survivor Series premium live event on Nov. 28.

According to WrestleVotes of Fightful Wrestling , those who are familiar with WWE's future plans do not believe The Rock will wrestle "anytime soon."

However, it was noted that many within the company were surprised by the announcement that The Rock will be at Survivor Series, leading WrestleVotes to admit that plans could potentially change as a result.

During an appearance Wednesday on the Pat McAfee Show , The Rock said, "I would not miss next week for the world, man. So, I'm going to Houston. Houston, we don't have a problem. I'm going to Houston and I'm gonna go to Survivor Series."

The Rock showing up at Survivor Series is fitting since it will mark the 30th anniversary of him making his WWE debut as Rocky Maivia at Survivor Series 1996.

It has been over a year and a half since The Rock last appeared on WWE programming at Elimination Chamber back in March 2025.

The Rock attempted to get Cody Rhodes to agree to sell him his soul at that event, but when Rhodes refused, John Cena shockingly turned heel and joined The Rock and rapper Travis Scott in attacking Rhodes.

It was widely assumed by most fans that The Rock would be a significant part of the build toward the WrestleMania 41 match between Rhodes and Cena after that, but he disappeared from WWE programming instead and left things entirely up to Rhodes and Cena.

The time since The Rock's last WWE match has been even longer, as that occurred at WrestleMania 40 in 2024.

Using the Final Boss moniker, The Rock teamed with Roman Reigns to beat Rhodes and Seth Rollins in a tag team bout that served as the Night 1 main event.

It initially looked like The Rock would be facing Reigns in a singles match at WrestleMania 40, but when fans made it clear they wanted Reigns vs. Rhodes, WWE went in a different direction.

The Rock vs. Reigns is still a match wanted by plenty of fans and arguably the biggest dream match WWE can possibly deliver.

WrestleMania 43 in Saudi Arabia could be the ideal stage for that contest, but all signs point toward a Reigns vs. Oba Femi match instead.

The possibility exists that The Rock could involve himself in the WarGames match between The Bloodline and 946 at Survivor Series to set something up for the future, but based on WrestleVotes' report, that may not be in the cards.

Colorado heads on the road for the final time this season, facing a struggling Cincinnati Bearcats team. The Bearcats have lost five of their last six games and have been very vulnerable against opponents' rushing attacks.

The Bearcats play their regular season finale on the road against BYU. CU needs to win its final two games to reach six wins.

In a game that is likely to be decide by two rushing attacks, here's how our Buffaloes Wire staff predicts Saturday's matchup will unfold.

Colorado vs. Cincinnati score predictions

They ran the ball better against Houston than in any other game this season. The Buffaloes also won the turnover battle, something that has been difficult for them this season. However, Cincinnati is also struggling with turnovers, and given their three-game losing streak, including their 28-point loss to Iowa State, this is a vulnerable offense Colorado can take advantage of. It will not be easy, but the Buffaloes ultimately escape this game with a win.

Charlie's prediction: Colorado's upset of Houston showed what its offense is capable of. The question has always been: can they put up a similar type of performance week in and week out? Against a Cincinnati team that just gave up over 285 rushing yards to Iowa State, I can finally say I see a path for the momentum to continue. The Bearcats have one of the Big 12's worst rushing defenses, giving Richard Young and JaQuail Smith another opportunity to take over. The key lies on the other side of the ball: a matchup between Cincinnati's rushing attack led by running back Cole Tabb and dual-threat quarterback JC French IV. I expect a high-scoring, back-and-forth contest, but Colorado's newfound offensive confidence and desperation to reach bowl eligibility will make the difference.

articles.title: Rangers injury updates: Durzi options; Dorofeyev, Smits, Veleno status
articles.summary: Sean Durzi was a full participant when the New York Rangers returned to practice Thursday, and appears to be trending […]
articles.body:
Sean Durzi was a full participant when the New York Rangers returned to practice Thursday, and appears to be trending toward a lineup return Sunday against the Carolina Hurricanes.

The 28-year-old defenseman missed the previous eight games with an unspecified injury , one that he labored through for a bit before landing on IR. The Rangers won six of eight games without their second-pair defenseman, though coach Mike Sullivan stated emphatically on Thursday that, "I don't think there's any question that he makes us a better team when he's in our lineup."

Durzi has five points (two goals, three assists) in 14 games, and is second among Rangers regulars , averaging 4.52 blocked shots per 60 minutes. He's also an important member of the League's top-ranked penalty-killing unit (89.7 percent), and quarterbacks the second power-play unit.

"When 'Durz' gets back in the lineup, I think he's going to bring what he's brought us since he's been here. He's just a solid two-way defenseman," Sullivan explained. "He's mobile guy. He helps get us out of our end, moves the puck, goes tape to tape. He's good along the offensive blue lien, he defends pretty well with his mobility and stick."

Durzi rotated in with the top-six defensemen at practice, though didn't get the first reps. That could change, and very likely will, over the next two days if he remains healthy as the Rangers ramp back up during a five-day break in the schedule .

Sullivan said that the coaches are still discussing what the Rangers defense corps will look like when Durzi returns to the lineup . Very likely, he'll assume his regular spot on the second pair next to Marcus Pettersson. Braden Schneider , who bumped up to fill in there during Durzi's absence, is expected to move back to the third pair.

But will Schneider remain on his right side or move to his (off) side? Scott Morrow 's played very well the past eight games since drawing into the lineup, and just scored his first goal with the Rangers in the 3-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens on Monday.

If Morrow remains in the lineup, that leaves the Rangers with four right-hand shots on the blue line, not exactly Sullivan's comfort zone. But he did say that's a possibility when Durzi comes back, though he didn't say which righty could shift to the other side.

If the Rangers do go with four righties, that means Matthew Robertson comes out of the lineup. The 25-year-old lefty has averaged just under 13 minutes TOI since replacing the injured Alberts Smits on the third defense pairing.

"What group of players gives us the best chance to win? If that means somebody's got to play their off side or off wing and we've got to move someone … then we'll make those decisions," the coach said.

Rangers provide updates on injured regulars Smits, Dorofeyev, Veleno

Speaking of Smits, who remains week to week with an upper-body injury, the 18-year-old rookie skated prior to practice with New York's skills coach. That's a step in the right direction for sure, but Sullivan didn't provide any more of an updated timeline on his expected return.

Pavel Dorofeyev skated on his own before practice and is day to day with a lower-body injury. The 26-year-old forward missed his first game of the season Monday, after leaving practice early the day before. Dorofeyev's had a rocky start to his Rangers tenure, after coming over from the Vegas Golden Knights in a draft-day trade in June and then signing a seven-year, $77 million contract. The two-time 30-goal scorer is tied for fifth on the Rangers with six goals and is a team-worst minus-18.

Will Cuylle , who scored two goals against the Canadiens after moving into the top-six forward group with Dorofeyev out Monday, remained on J.T. Miller 's line at practice Thursday. Matt Rempe , who drew back into the lineup Monday, practiced in the same spot on the fourth line.

Then there's Joe Veleno, who played only four games this season and is expected to be out until mid-January or so due to a lower-body injury.

"Joe Veleno is going through his rehab off the ice. My understanding is that he has not gone on the ice yet (confirmed)," Sullivan explained.

Glenn Gawdin and Luke Glendening took turns centering the fourth line at practice, following two off days for the team.

articles.title: Patriots Cut A.J. Brown Losses Before Trade Disaster Deepens
articles.summary: A.J. Brown's latest injury and poor stats make Bill Simmons' harsh trade critique look right. The Patriots must cut their losses now.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown will miss time with a hamstring injury, and the Patriots cannot wait much longer to act. Reports from ESPN's Jeremy Fowler indicate the star receiver will be out "a little while" after getting hurt against the Detroit Lions. This news comes on top of a season that has already turned into a nightmare for New England fans.

The trade that brought Brown to Foxborough looks like a mistake. Bill Simmons called the deal "one of the worst trades in Boston sports history" on his podcast. He said the move was a disaster after Brown played just four games. The former tight end Rob Gronkowski agreed with that harsh take. "It's been a disappointment, you know, the disappointing trade so far," Gronkowski said. Brown has caught only 11 passes for 128 yards and has zero touchdowns this year.

To acquire him, New England surrendered a 2028 first-round pick along with a 2027 fifth-round pick. Since the player is injured once more, that cost now seems significantly greater. Brown has dealt with a high-ankle sprain, a nagging knee issue, and now this hamstring setback. These assorted injuries caused him to miss six of the initial nine games. The team sent a first-rounder for a player who is not at 100 percent on a dreadful Munich field. It is hard to see how the math works for the Patriots here.

Former NFL GM Ran Carthon believes the team should not hold on to this contract. While Brown's contract extends until the 2029 season, his guaranteed base salary for 2027 totals only $4 million. Carthon told CBS that the team needs to stop trying to prove they were right. "You don't want to compound a mistake by holding on to it too long … you cut your losses," Carthon said. He stressed that good teams admit when a draft pick or trade is not working and move on quickly.

The offense is already in trouble without Brown. NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler noted in an ESPN piece that Brown's injury was not just a precaution. "Where the offense turns next is fascinating," Fowler wrote. The team also lost Drake Maye to a fractured ankle for the rest of the 2026 season. TreVeyon Henderson is on injured reserve for at least three more games. Rhamondre Stevenson is also banged up with a knee injury. The trade deadline has passed, so the team cannot add instant fixes.

Coach Mike Vrabel defended Brown's effort in practice before Sunday's game. "I thought he had a good week of practice," Vrabel said of Brown. Yet the results on the field tell a different story. The Patriots sit at 5-5 and enter their bye week with a fractured roster. Facing the Los Angeles Chargers on November 29, Brown gets two weeks to recover first.

articles.title: Bucks’ Brayden Burries gets thoroughly cooked by fans for what-if Heat game scenario
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Bucks continued their torrid run at the start of the season when they took on the Miami Heat at the Kaseya Center in what was a one-off GTA-the...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Bucks continued their torrid run at the start of the season when they took on the Miami Heat at the Kaseya Center in what was a one-off GTA-themed event. Milwaukee lost 137-130 to drop to an NBA-worst 1-14 record as Giannis Antetokounmpo scored a game-high of 27 points in a double-double alongside 14 rebounds and nine assists in his first game against his former team since leaving.

However, rookie Brayden Burries had a grounded explanation behind why Milwaukee ended up losing against the Heat, per a post on X by Heat Central.

"It was a great game plan," he said. "They just made 3s tonight. If they don't make half their 3s then we probably win tonight"

Burries will undoubtedly be disappointed with how his life in the NBA have begun despite the lottery pick himself immediately becoming a regular contributor, averaging 10.1 points, 5.5 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game. However, the explanation was undoubtedly an "if my grandmother had wheels" moment as the Heat had effectively won the game in the first half after they returned with a 26-point advantage.

As a matter of fact, the Bucks were able to save themselves from a blowout due to a 44-25 fourth quarter, which came after Miami had already begun to bench starters. As one would expect, a range of fans immediately began to troll Burries as they begane to explain exactly how the Heat had dominated Milwaukee for much of the game.

"1-14. Down most of the game by 25. And this is what he says. Lol," one fan wrote .

Miami were leading by 30 points at one point and were fairly confident that they would get the win by the second half, as another fan pointed out .

"son, its a 30 points lead in the 4th before they give you some momentum to save face," they wrote.

Another user simply found humor in Burries' comment, writing the following.

"if they missed their shots tonight and we made ours we would've won," they said.

Still, it is fair to see exactly what Burries meant. The Heat's three-point shooting has been regularly questioned and they undoubtedly do not have a lot of shooters outside of Klay Thompson and Davion Mitchell, especially considering the interior threat of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo.

Still, Miami managed to convert 22 of their 45 attempts against Milwaukee, going an impressive 45.8% from beyond the arc, which was one of the many reasons why they ended up with an easy win.

articles.title: Texas high school changes football workouts after players are hospitalized
articles.summary: Six Frenship Memorial football players were hospitalized with rhabdo symptoms. Frenship ISD has changed workouts and notified CPS.
articles.body:
Several Texas high school football players were hospitalized after an offseason workout last week, with one reportedly requiring intensive care.

A Chron report said six players from Frenship Memorial High School in Lubbock were hospitalized with symptoms of rhabdomyolysis, a potentially life-threatening condition caused by the breakdown of muscle tissue. Amanda Blacklund, a physician at Lubbock Primary Care Center, told the outlet that six players were admitted for treatment, including one reportedly in intensive care.

In a statement included in the report, Frenship ISD confirmed that several players continue to receive treatment and said district officials are investigating what may have contributed to their conditions.

The district also reported the situation to Child Protective Services for investigation.

Frenship ISD has since reduced the intensity of its offseason football workouts and expanded education for coaches and players about hydration, nutrition, rest and recognizing symptoms of rhabdomyolysis.

The condition occurs when damaged muscle tissue releases substances into the bloodstream, potentially causing severe kidney damage or failure. It can be triggered by extreme physical exertion.

Frenship Memorial, which opened in 2025, is coached by Jason Richards. The Panthers finished their 2026 football season with a 2-8 record.

The district has not released additional details about the affected players, citing privacy concerns.

articles.title: Stanford’s $50M Rebuild Meets Cal’s Coaching Uncertainty in Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Stanford can become bowl-eligible for the first time since 2018.
articles.body:
Cal and Stanford will meet this Saturday in the 129th iteration of the Big Game, as each program continues to find its footing in the new college football landscape.

Stanford (5–5, 3–4) picked up its most impressive win of the season last Saturday, a convincing 40–22 victory over Virginia Tech (6–4, 3–4). The win snapped a program-record 15-game losing streak on the road. The losing streak was also the longest active streak in the FBS.

The Cardinal are one win away from bowl eligibility for the first time since 2018 under program alum and first-year coach Tavita Pritchard. Stanford's resurgence comes against the backdrop of significant financial investment into the program, beginning with a $50 million gift last October. What followed in 2026 was a series of partnerships to advance its NIL (name, image, and likeness) efforts including a jersey patch partnership deal with DoorDash in September, the largest sponsorship deal in Stanford athletics history.

Conversely, Cal (3–7, 2–5) sits at the bottom of the ACC standings and is on a four-game losing streak. The Golden Bears are also led by a program alum in his first year in Tosh Lupoi; however a tumultuous season has led to questions about his long-term security despite signing a five-year contract last December.

As Saturday looms, each coach needs a win to validate what they're building, with an added layer of motivation given the history of this rivalry matchup.

"The other truth is this game may feel a little different," Pritchard said to local reporters this week. "You have to be able to hold that and you have to be aware of that and even lean into it here a little bit this week."

Stanford was one of college football's most successful programs from 2010 to 2018, winning 94 games and six bowl games. Since then, the program won 24 games prior to this season with three different head coaches. Program legend Andrew Luck took over as the school's first general manager in November 2024. He fired coach Troy Taylor in March 2025 amid reports of Taylor's inappropriate behavior towards women on the athletic staff. Taylor subsequently filed a defamation lawsuit against ESPN for its reporting on the matter, which a federal court dismissed in March 2026.

Luck hired Frank Reich as a one-year interim coach as he sought a program reset. The Cardinal went 4–8 in 2025, the program's fifth consecutive losing season, but a $50 million gift from program alum Bradford M. Freeman that October was a positive sign. In a school issued-statement , the gift will be used to build institutional NIL funds and add new scholarships, as FBS football rosters can now carry 105 players. It's the largest non-facilities gift in Stanford football history.

"The Division I athletics environment is rapidly changing," Stanford Jaquish & Kenninger Director and Chair of Athletics John Donahue told Front Office Sports ."Competitive excellence at the highest level now requires significant institutional support, along with identifying creative opportunities for external organizations to engage."

Stanford's investment into a new financial, football infrastructure continued in 2026 with several new ventures:

May 2026: Signed a multiyear partnership with Ramp to oversee expense management over all 36 varsity programs.

August 2026: Signed a multiyear sponsorship deal with Fortinet, for naming rights to the Director's Level, the premier hospitality area at home football games as well as branding in the end zone.

September 2026: Signed a corporate sponsorship with DoorDash as the official jersey patch sponsor of Stanford athletics, the largest sponsorship agreement in Stanford athletics history.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, Stanford announced another partnership with Redwood Brand Partners , an independent NIL organization that will connect Stanford athletes with prospective organizations for short-term and long-term sponsorship opportunities.

"We are dedicated to supporting and empowering our student-athletes through revenue sharing and a strong, sustainable NIL ecosystem," Donahue said. "Every decision we make regarding NIL is predicated on optimizing the student-athlete experience with an intentional approach that is authentically Stanford: ambitious, thoughtful, and focused on long-term development."

On the field, Stanford's five wins have already surpassed any win total since 2018. Pritchard, Luck's teammate at Stanford from 2008-2009, has yielded good results in year one. There's a renewed confidence in Stanford's trajectory under Luck's leadership.

"Andrew's leadership has been evident since day one and his passion for this program, and, more importantly, our university, is unmatched," Donahue said. "It's been rewarding to watch Andrew lead in his general manager role, and he has great instincts when it comes to being more hands-on or knowing when to delegate.

"His ability to inspire and build relationships is second to none. I have truly enjoyed working alongside Andrew and he has also been a trusted resource during my transition to the department last year."

With one more win, Stanford can accomplish a goal it's pursued since the beginning of the season: a bowl game berth. As the program investments continue, the larger goal is returning the program back to national prominence, this time as a member of the ACC, which the Cardinal joined in 2024.

"We've made no bones about playing for an extra game," Pritchard said after the victory over Virginia Tech. "We're one step closer to that. With this team, we've gotten better every single game. We want to be a team that is better today than we were yesterday and better next week than we were this week."

Cal hired Lupoi as its head coach last December after a successful stint as Oregon's defensive coordinator. However, his job status might be in question after just 10 games. The speculation around his security heightened earlier this month when school general manager and fellow program alum Ron Rivera was very critical of Lupoi's first year as coach during a media appearance on the local KNBR radio station.

"Tosh came in as a first-time head coach. He did bring a couple of inexperienced coordinators with him," Rivera said. "Things didn't work out the way we needed them to work out on offense.

"He has bumped his head a lot. We have talked a lot, tried to give him a lot of advice, point him in the right direction. Some of it, he's been very receptive, and other portions of it, he hasn't. And it's those things that sometimes you've gotta learn for yourself before you think, ' Oh wow, this is it.'

"But now it's time. These last three games, hopefully four, the trajectory has to be going north."

Lupoi hired two first-time coordinators in Jordan Somerville (offense) and Michael Hutchings (defense). Somerville has since been stripped of his play-calling duties as Cal is ranked 122nd nationally in scoring offense and 106th in yards per game. The defense hasn't fared much better, ranking 123rd in scoring defense and 110th in yards allowed per game.

Following Rivera's comments on Nov. 5, he and Lupoi held a joint press conference on Nov. 11 in an attempt to smooth any speculation and present a united front. Lupoi's total guaranteed compensation is $22.6 million, or $4.5 million annually. His buyout is 80% of his remaining contract which equates to $14.5 million.

"I'd say the biggest thing is we can't control what's behind us and, yeah, it has been disappointing," Rivera said during the joint press conference. "But what I'm really excited about is the way the approach has been for what's in front of us. We have an opportunity to go out and do some really special things.

"We've got three games left, they're all against ACC opponents and I think the work and the development and the growth is what we're looking at."

articles.title: 2 MLB Players Accept Qualifying Offers Worth $23.15 Million For 2027
articles.summary: Two of the eight MLB players who received qualifying offers accepted and will remain with their teams for 2027: David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twin...
articles.body:
2015 marked the first year that any MLB player accepted a qualifying offer ("QO"). Three players did it: Brett Anderson accepted $15.8 million from the Los Angeles Dodgers, Colby Rasmus did the same with the Houston Astros, and Matt Wieters did said "yes" to the Baltimore Orioles.

Ten years later, the record was set with four players accepting their QOs : Brandon Woodruff (Milwaukee Brewers), Shota Imanaga (Chicago Cubs), Gleyber Torres (Detroit Tigers), and Trent Grisham (New York Yankees).

This year eight players were given QOs. With the MLB's financial system potentially in flux, as owners prepare to lock out the players when the current collective bargaining agreement expires at midnight on December 1 st , and with there no way of knowing if the QO will even exist in the new CBA, there was a lot of uncertainty about whether any of these players would accept what amounts to a one-year, $23.15 million contract.

This week we got the answer: reliever David Bednar and catcher Ryan Jeffers both said "yes."

Tim Britton of The Athletic had predicted that Bednar would receive a three-year deal worth $57 million. MLB Trade Rumors had four years, $68 million. Both of those deals would have been less on an average annual basis than he received by accepting the QO, but certainly more guaranteed. Like Grisham last year, one wonders if the Yankees now regret making the offer to Bednar, as this probably takes them out of the running for free agent reliever Adrián Morejón, who could have become New York's new closer (and, who, ironically, became a free agent because he rejected a QO from San Diego).

As for Jeffers, his agent, Scott Boras, went on a long and convoluted journey at last week's general managers' meetings trying to extol the virtues of his client and how he could be an asset to any team.

"A right-handed bat and a catcher, it's kind of a constellation. It's a talent. It's something that pretty much creates kind of a star skill market for players at that position. "A lot of teams are kind of going, 'Oh-Ryan is certainly something that will put more championship notches in my belt.'"

Well, Jeffers simply undercut all of that gibberish and accepted Minnesota's offer. Coincidentally, by taking the QO, Jeffers now has the highest average annual value for any catcher ever, just eclipsing the $23.1 million that J.T. Realmuto received in his five-year, $115.5 million deal with Philadelphia in 2021, and the $23 million per year – for eight years – that Joe Mauer agreed to with those same Twins back in 2011. Obviously, the extra $50,000 is nothing compared to the massive guarantees that both Realmuto and Mauer received. Jeffers will turn 30 on June 3, so he will become a free agent again going into his age-31 season. But, from an OPS+ perspective, his production has gone up each of the past three years, and he has averaged more than 2 bWAR over the past four seasons. He can still catch and handle a pitching staff, so that should continue to have value in the coming years.

By accepting the QO, Jeffers gets to remain someplace he is comfortable while he (and the rest of the league) waits out the labor impasse, knowing that he has a (and remains) home for at least another year and gets to catch one of the best pitching staffs in the American League.

To date, there has been no discussion about the qualifying offer concept going away in the new CBA, so we may be right back here again next season, trying to determine who will take big short-term money and who will roll the dice in free agency.

articles.title: Detroit Tigers Face Major Zach McKinstry Decision Before Friday Deadline
articles.summary: Detroit has until Friday to decide on Zach McKinstry, and the price is what makes it hard. #Tigers
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers have until Friday at 5 p.m. ET to tender a 2027 contract to infielder Zach McKinstry , and the price is what makes the deadline real. MLB Trade Rumors projects McKinstry for about $5 million in arbitration next season, which is a lot of money for a hitter coming off the year he just had. If Detroit does not tender him, he becomes a free agent.

The Money Behind the Zach McKinstry Decision

That projection is not a signed salary. It is the number arbitration would be expected to land on, and it sits on top of a season at the plate that went badly. In 2026 McKinstry played 129 games for Detroit, hitting .199 with four home runs and 26 RBIs. He stole three bases in eight attempts and finished with a .288 on-base percentage.

Detroit Tigers Are Better Off Not Tending Zach McKinstry

At that price, it does not make sense for Detroit to keep him as a utility man. The Tigers are better off finding utility help elsewhere, and the 40-man roster spot matters here as much as the dollars do.

The defense is the argument on the other side. McKinstry won the 2026 Fielding Bible Award for multi-position play, and Sports Info Solutions credited him with 13 Defensive Runs Saved in right field alone across 62 games there, third among right fielders. He also appeared at second base, shortstop, third base, all three outfield spots and pitcher. Two years ago he was an All-Star , added to the American League roster in July 2025 as a replacement for Jeremy Peña.

A trade before Friday is the other way this ends. National writers have floated the New York Yankees as a fit for that versatility, and DSN ran a trade proposal along those lines earlier this month. That is outside speculation: no trade talks involving McKinstry have been reported.

articles.title: Kings captain Drew Doughty makes major agent move in contract year
articles.summary: It has been a difficult season for the Los Angeles Kings. They are 6-11-2 this year, sitting in seventh place in the Pacific Division. They also have new lea...
articles.body:
It has been a difficult season for the Los Angeles Kings . They are 6-11-2 this year, sitting in seventh place in the Pacific Division. They also have new leadership on the ice. Longtime captain Anze Kopitar retired at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, and Drew Doughty is now the captain of the team. Still, Doughty's tenure as the captain could be short-lived. He is in the final year of an eight-year deal he signed with the Kings in 2018. Doughty has said he wants to continue playing until he is 40 , but he will need a new contract to do so.

Now, the 36-year-old defenseman has made a move regarding his contract, according to Pierre LeBrun of TSN.

"Pending UFA Drew Doughty just shared with reporters here in Toronto that he's hired Pat Brisson of CAA Sports as his agent. Doughty had gone many years without an agent. But obviously will need to negotiate a new contract, whether that's in LA or elsewhere. He made it clear he hopes to stay with the Kings," LeBrun posted on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Doughty was the second overall pick of the 2008 NHL Draft by the Kings and broke into the NHL with the team that season. He has played 1,297 games with the franchise, scoring 166 goals and adding 551 assists. He is also a five-time All-Star, a two-time member of the NHL second All-Star team, and a two-time Stanley Cup champion.

His new agent, Pat Brisson, is one of the most influential agents in the NHL. He often represents big-time players. His list of clients includes Hall of Famers Mario Lemieux, Martin Brodeur, and Luc Robitaille. Meanwhile, Brisson has represented such stars as Sidney Crosby, Nathan MacKinnon, Macklin Celebrini, Gavin McKenna, and all three of the Hughes brothers.

While Doughty has made moves off the ice, he is also looking to help his team get back to winning on the ice. The Kings have lost four of their last five, but have a chance to get back into the win column when they visit the Toronto Maple Leafs on Thursday night.

articles.title: Luke Humphries shocked by Tom Sykes in last-leg thriller at Grand Slam of Darts a day after Luke Littler exit
articles.summary: Luke Humphries is out at the last 16 stage of the Grand Slam after losing to Tom Sykes; Humphries was struggling with a trapped nerve in his shoulder; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22
articles.body:
It is the second big shock in the space of two days following world No 1 Luke Littler's loss to Jermaine Wattimena. Now, with the world No 2 also out, the competition is well and truly blown wide open.

Humphries looked to be struggling with a problem in his shoulder throughout the contest but managed to find some strong darts to take the contest all the way.

But Sykes, who is now ranked 72nd in the world, held on and prevailed to pick up the biggest win of his career and reach his first ever major quarter-final.

It means Humphries will have to wait to try and clinch his second Grand Slam title following his victory back in 2023.

"I was a bit nervous, but obviously I thought the game was over when I turned around and saw Luke hit the first treble 18 there, and hit the second one and then wired it," Sykes told Sky Sports following his win.

"I was so cold on that last one. I just thought, just hit it first out, no messing about, and get into it. And I did.

"I'm just riding a wave at the minute. I'm not really bothered who I play. I'll just come back up here and we'll see what happens."

For Sykes, a mouth-watering clash with Michael van Gerwen awaits after he came through with a remarkable contest against James Wade with a 10-8 victory.

It marks Van Gerwen's first ranking quarter-final of 2026 and he earned it in some style with a near 104 average. There was nothing separating two darting juggernauts throughout the high-quality bout, a massive 121 checkout from the Dutchman levelling the game at 7-7 before rattling off two more legs to move 9-7 ahead.

Wade did not give up and a stunning 130 checkout, his second of the match, broke Van Gerwen's throw but the three-time Grand Slam champion broke straight back and pinned D16 for the win.

"To play in these types of games was even worse. I made it incredibly difficult for myself. That's sometimes so annoying," Van Gerwen told Sky Sports .

"I couldn't hit a double after the second break and with James Wade standing behind me - it's so annoying - but it's also his class. I dealt with it the right way, and now I feel comfortable now.

Sykes made it clear he would be making the match a real contest in the first session. He averaged 107.42 in a staggering opening five legs that saw him win four with incredible ease against the in-form player in the darting world.

Although still looking uncomfortable, Humphries fought back as Sykes went slightly off the boil. That saw him pick up four of the next five legs to level the game at 5-5.

The game continued to go back and forth as Humphries found some of his top levels, but Sykes would not back down, fighting back despite some strong finishing from 'Cool Hand', a 114 finish on tops the highlight.

It then looked like it was all going to go the way of Humphries when he powered in back-to-back 11-darters to take the game to a final-leg showdown but the 'Castleford Tiger' showed why he has become a formidable player.

Humphries missed D10 to finish off a 128 checkout which allowed Sykes to have his match dart at 36. He pinned that first dart for a win to remember.

Humphries took to social media after the contest to congratulate Sykes and admitted he has been through a tough 48 hours.

Humphries said: "Well done Tom Sykes absolutely amazing performance!

"So proud of the way I played tonight with what I've had to go through with injury the last 48 hours gave it my absolute all there.

"Wish everyone all the best for the rest of the tournament."

The moment Sykes sealed his last eight spot

Sykes has been on the darting circuit since 2013 when he competed on the PDC Challenge Tour and then followed that up with a year on the PDC Development Tour.

It is over the last two years that Sykes has truly flourished. He qualified for the 2025 UK Open and made it all the way to the third round.

Earlier this year he clinched his Tour card at Q-School and has since made it to the fourth round at the UK Open before picking up the win of his career with the scalp of the world No 2 on the Grand Slam stage.

The 34-year-old hails from Castleford in West Yorkshire and his nickname 'The Castleford Tiger' is an ode to the rugby league side from his hometown.

Nathan Aspinall made it through to the quarter-finals with a hard-fought 10-7 victory over Gabriel Clemens.

Aspinall apologised post-match for "writing off" the German player before the game and it was clear why, with Clemens averaging 96.55 and hitting 10 180s.

It was a topsy-turvy game throughout the first two sessions and at the end of them, the scores were level at 5-5.

However, it was from there that Aspinall took control. From 6-5 down, he took out four legs in a row and found a massive 'Big Fish' finish for a break of throw to send the Wolverhampton crowd wild.

Clemens did manage to get one more leg on the board but in the 17th leg, Aspinall scored highly and clinched D16 for a spot in the last eight.

He will take on Gian van Veen after he held off a fightback from Martin Schindler for a 10-7 win.

It was in the second session that the world No 3 stepped things up. Averaging over 104, he took advantage of Schindler's clear issues on the doubles to take out four of the five legs to be 7-3 ahead.

Van Veen then made that seven out of eight legs and was one leg from victory before a period of poor scoring for the third seed and a massive improvement from Schindler saw the German take out four legs to put the pressure on.

Eventually, Van Veen found back-to-back 134s and took out 93 to book the showdown with Aspinall.

articles.title: Tom Sykes ready to go 'all the way' on debut at Grand Slam of Darts after defeating Luke Humphries
articles.summary: Tom Sykes came up with a thrilling 10-9 victory over Luke Humphries at the Grand Slam of Darts; It sees him through to the quarter-finals on debut; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22
articles.body:
The 'Castleford Tiger', who is making his debut in Wolverhampton, put in an incredible performance against the world No 2 in which he raced away before 'Cool Hand' fought back to take the game to a last-leg decider.

Sykes scored amazingly in that winner-takes-all leg and with Humphries unable to finish off the 128 checkout, he clinched D18 to set up a quarter-final showdown with Michael van Gerwen after his 10-8 win over James Wade in the final match of the night.

Sykes is ranked 72nd in the world in what is his first year on the PDC Pro Tour but, with the way he is playing, he sees no reason why he cannot go on a real run at the Grand Slam.

"I think so. I know I have got the scoring game," Sykes said.

"I know I have got the scoring game to live with anyone in the world, and I have shown it tonight with the 180s and the 140s that I have been hitting.

"If the doubles go in, then I'm a dangerous player."

Humphries was suffering with a shoulder injury throughout the contest and Sykes did not realise until they were practicing and was gingerly picking up his darts.

Despite the clear pain Humphries was in, Sykes still feels he was up against the best darts player in the world playing some of the best darts in the world.

"I can't believe it, honestly. Luke didn't tell me till the end, but he said he had a bit of an injury there. I could tell, to be fair," he added.

"In the practice darts at the beginning, he was dropping his darts and he could barely bend over to pick them up.

"He still played really well and I got off to a really good start. To get 4-1 up against, in my opinion, the best player in the world at the minute, I'm absolutely buzzing with that.

"For me, he is still one of the best players in the world, even if he's injured or not. I am just buzzing to get the win over him."

'I was watching them on TV, now I an practicing with them'

Many a player would be overawed with the experiences that Sykes is now having but, as someone who enjoys the big stages, he is revelling in rubbing shoulders with the top stars of the sport.

"When I first started on the Pro Tour and I'm walking in, you see Luke Humphries, Luke Littler, Michael van Gerwen, James Wade. It is a bit daunting walking in and seeing all these guys who you've watched on TV," Sykes said.

"I have been in there tonight and I've been playing with Gian van Veen and with James Wade. You are like, 'what am I doing in here with these lot?'

"Now I am mixing it with these on the big stages, it is mad.

"I have always said that I am a big stage player, I like playing on big stages.

"I massively put the hard work in for the last year, and I ended up getting my Tour card last year, and now I'm reaping the rewards of it."
