articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts 2026: Luke Humphries upset by unseeded Tom Sykes in second round
articles.summary: Luke Humphries follows Luke Littler in exiting the Grand Slam of Darts after losing 10-9 to unseeded Tom Sykes in a second-round thriller.
articles.body:
Luke Humphries followed Luke Littler in exiting the Grand Slam of Darts after losing 10-9 to unseeded Tom Sykes in a second-round thriller.

Having trailed 4-0 and 9-7, the second seed battled back to force a deciding leg and had the advantage of throwing first.

But his fellow Englishman Sykes was unfazed, quickly took control of the leg and when Humphries missed double 10 for a 128 checkout to snatch victory, the world number 81 nervelessly hit double 18 to secure a place in his first major quarter-final.

"It's unbelievable," Sykes, 34, told Sky Sports. "Luke let me off a few times in the first bit but I set off really well.

"When he got it back to 5-5, I thought 'here we go' and he started turning it on in the last 10 legs, but I'm just buzzing to get over the line.

"I was a bit nervous [going for double 18 for the match]. I thought the game was over when I saw Luke hit the the first treble 18, then the second.

"But I was so cold on that last one, I thought 'just hit it first dart, no messing about' and I did. I'm riding a wave at the minute and I'll keep trying to ride it."

Sykes' victory was all the more impressive given Humphries did not play badly at all, averaging 102.02 and hitting 37% on the doubles.

But the Castleford thrower made a flying start, averaging just shy of 108 in the first mini-session, to earn a sizeable lead and maintained his composure as the former world champion fought back.

He will face three-time Grand Slam champion Michael van Gerwen in the last eight after the Dutchman beat seventh seed James Wade 10-8.

In a high-class contest that saw six 100-plus finishes, Wade earned a 7-5 lead but Van Gerwen, who finished with an average of 103.83, took out 121 to level at 7-7.

He broke again to go 9-7 up and although Wade hit a 130 checkout to break back, 10th seed Van Gerwen made it three breaks in a row to avoid a one-leg shootout.

With Humphries and Littler gone, third seed Gian van Veen is the top-ranked player remaining in the draw in Wolverhampton.

The Dutchman beat Germany's Martin Schindler 10-7 and was completely dominant before a slight wobble as he tried to close out the win.

Van Veen raced into a 9-3 lead but then proceeded to lose four legs on the spin, missing three match darts, before eventually finishing the job.

England's Nathan Aspinall awaits last year's World Championship finalist in the quarters after a 10-7 win over German Gabriel Clemens.

'The Asp' averaged 100.72 and posted an impressive 53% checkout rate as he came out on top in a back-and-forth match.

articles.title: Nolan Wells murder case: Grand jury reveals shocking findings after reviewing evidence from 43 witnesses
articles.summary: The investigation into Nolan Wells’ death has reached a major turning point, but it has not answered every question surrounding the 18-year-old’s final
articles.body: The investigation into Nolan Wells’ death has reached a major turning point, but it has not answered every question surrounding the 18-year-old’s final hours. A Mississippi grand jury has concluded that the evidence does not support criminal charges against anyone connected to his July 4 disappearance. The decision follows weeks of public scrutiny, online accusations and calls for answers from people following the case. While the panel believes drowning best explains Wells’ death, several details remain uncertain, including how he sustained a head injury before his body was found.Nolan Wells death: Grand jury finds no evidence of criminal activityThe Jackson County Grand Jury reviewed evidence from 43 witnesses before reaching its decision. Its investigation included police reports, interviews, photographs, videos, digital records, maps and physical evidence gathered during the search and recovery operation.Wells disappeared after celebrating Independence Day with friends on barrier islands off Mississippi’s Gulf Coast. Search teams recovered his body near Horn Island two days later.The grand jury report stated that the "position of, condition of, time of discovery, and location" of his body was "consistent with drowning." It also said there was "no credible evidence to support the public allegations" that anyone aboard the boats involved in the trip had committed a crime connected to his death.The panel found no evidence of a fatal injury or underlying disease. Investigators did identify bruising on the back of Wells’ head, but said it was "not a fatal injury." One witness described seeing him "slip awkwardly off the side of a boat" around the time he was last seen. However, the witness could not confirm whether Wells hit his head.The report also found no evidence of a physical fight or argument involving Wells that day.Nolan Wells case leaves unanswered questions despite grand jury decisionThe toxicology findings offered limited clarity. According to the report, decomposition made it difficult to assess substance levels reliably. However, the panel found no cocaine in Wells’ system and no evidence that he had previously used the drug.The investigation also addressed speculation about Wells’ missing phone. The grand jury said it was not unusual for people to return from the island on different boats or leave personal belongings on vessels they visited. It also noted that Wells’ phone was not the only device to return to the mainland without its owner.The report strongly criticised the public accusations directed at people connected to the trip and their families. It described those attacks as "malicious, false, and have no truth in fact or evidence."Despite closing the door on criminal charges for now, the grand jury left room for future action. Mississippi has no statute of limitations on homicide cases. The report said that if credible evidence suggests Wells’ death was non-accidental, the matter should return to the grand jury for further review.For now, the decision brings a legal conclusion, but not every answer Wells’ family and the public have been seeking.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Floyd Mayweather gets relief as Las Vegas prosecutors drop two felony charges in $200,000 watch case
articles.summary: Floyd Mayweather Jr. will no longer face two felony charges in Las Vegas over an alleged $200,000 check used to buy a luxury watch.
articles.body: Floyd Mayweather Jr. will no longer face two felony charges in Las Vegas over an alleged $200,000 check used to buy a luxury watch. Prosecutors asked the court to dismiss the case, and the charges were dropped on Wednesday, November 18, according to court records reported by The Associated Press. The case had raised questions about the boxer’s finances, but its end gives him relief from this criminal matter. The watch was returned to the Las Vegas store, and the district attorney’s office said both sides were satisfied.Floyd Mayweather’s $200,000 watch case ends after store gets the watch backThe case began with a purchase made on December 31, 2024. According to the criminal complaint, Mayweather bought an Audemars Piguet watch from Gold and Beyond, a designer resale store in Las Vegas. Prosecutors said he paid with a $200,000 check from a Wells Fargo account, but the payment was not covered by enough money in the account.The complaint led to two felony counts being filed in April 2026. One accused Mayweather of theft involving property worth $100,000 or more. The other accused him of drawing or passing a check worth at least $1,200 with the intent to defraud.These were allegations, not findings of guilt. If the case had gone to trial, prosecutors would have had to prove the charges. Mayweather’s legal team had also denied that he intended to cheat the store.The store’s lawyer had earlier told ESPN that the owner trusted Mayweather and gave him time to resolve the payment issue. The lawyer claimed the owner eventually stopped receiving replies and had not been paid.The situation has now ended without a trial. Andryanna Sheppard, a public information officer for the Clark County District Attorney’s Office, told MMA Junkie that the watch had been returned and the two sides were satisfied.“Both parties are satisfied,” Sheppard told MMA Junkie. “Therefore, the State will be dismissing the case.”The Associated Press reported on November 18 that the court dismissed the charges at prosecutors’ request. A hearing set for November 19 was canceled. The AP said it had sought comments from Mayweather’s lawyer, prosecutors and the store’s lawyer.Floyd Mayweather still has other legal and financial issues to deal withThe dismissal removes this criminal case, but it does not mean every legal dispute involving Mayweather has ended. He is also involved in a separate fight with CSI Sports over a boxing event. The company has accused him of breaking a contract connected to a planned bout with Mike Tyson. Mayweather has denied the allegations in court filings.The dispute is separate from the Las Vegas watch case. It concerns a business agreement and does not involve the dismissed felony charges.Mayweather has also faced questions over an IRS tax lien reported at $7.3 million. Uncrowned reported that the lien was filed in April 2026 and related to unpaid taxes for 2018 and 2023. There has been no confirmed public update in the reports reviewed here showing that the lien has been paid or released.The two felony counts are no longer pending, and the November 19 hearing will not take place. But the dismissal is not a court ruling that the original allegations were false. The case ended after prosecutors asked to drop it and the watch was returned.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Divyanshi Bhowmick’s 16th birthday comes with a senior national crown and bigger dreams
articles.summary: MUMBAI: While turning 16 typically involves cakes, parties and celebrations with friends, for Divyanshi Bhowmick, the milestone came with a rather unusual
articles.body: MUMBAI: While turning 16 typically involves cakes, parties and celebrations with friends, for Divyanshi Bhowmick, the milestone came with a rather unusual gift, something she gave herself: a senior national title and a place in Indian table tennis history.On Tuesday, two days before her 16th birthday, the Maharashtra paddler became the youngest player to win a senior national title in the women’s section, clinching the women’s singles crown at the 3rd National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Punjab.A day after winning the women’s title, Divyanshi was back at the table competing in the girls’ category. She didn’t win that one, but it was hardly going to spoil her mood. After all, the senior crown was already safely in her bag, and she was geared up for her next assignment. “I think this title is really special for me because my main target this year is to get into the women’s team. I lost the final at the first zonal tournament, so I was really prepared to play better and win the title this time. Being the youngest-ever winner is also a special and proud moment for me,” she told TOI.The final against Tamil Nadu’s Ananya Muralidharan was a test of nerve as much as skill. Having already accounted for second seed Yashaswini Ghorpade in the semifinals, Divyanshi found herself pushed to the brink in the title clash. Trailing 7-10 in the deciding game, the teenager produced a stunning comeback, saving the situation before sealing a 14-12 victory. Despite having international titles to her name, including gold at the 2025 Asian Cadet Championships in Tashkent, where she became the first Indian in 36 years to win the girls’ U-15 singles crown, Divyanshi considers this her biggest achievement yet. The timing of the victory could hardly have been better. With the pathway to India’s senior team becoming increasingly competitive, national ranking tournaments have assumed greater significance.Under the current selection system, players ranked in the world’s top 30 earn direct entry, while the remaining places are contested through the domestic and international circuit. With no Indian woman currently in that elite bracket, the likes of Manika Batra and Sreeja Akula have also been turning up at national ranking events. For Divyanshi, that presents an opportunity rather than an intimidating challenge. She has seen 17-year-old Syndrela Das break through to the Asian Games squad and also earn a place at the Youth Olympics. She wants to follow a similar path.“Winning this title gives me a lot of confidence that I can keep winning more titles. All I want is to qualify for the Indian team,” she said. On Thursday, her birthday celebrations were brief. She had cut a cake with her family at midnight before heading to the airport for Istanbul, where she will represent India at the ITTF World Youth Championships.For now, the teenager will continue shuttling between youth and senior tournaments, chasing medals in one and a place in the Indian women’s team through the other. Her 16th birthday may have involved more air time than celebrations, perhaps in keeping with her goal of flying high.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Deion Sanders receives 'about five' death threats every day as Colorado football coach
articles.summary: Deion Sanders gets about five death threats a day, per The Athletic, which obtained 15 closed harassment cases since he took over Colorado football.
articles.body: Just a few years ago, Colorado’s football program had largely been forgotten. Then Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders arrived in Boulder, bringing his larger-than-life personality and celebrity to the program. Colorado’s on-field results under Sanders have been uneven, but his tenure has also been marked by significant off-field challenges. Sanders has continued coaching while managing serious health issues. More recently, police records obtained by The Athletic detailed how his personal safety has been at risk at times. According to a September report, Sanders regularly received death threats. At one point, he said he was receiving "about five" threats per day. Public records from Boulder shed light on how authorities handled many of those situations. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE In May 2023, a pair of university police officers waited for Sanders outside his office. Once the two-time Super Bowl winner met the officers, they told Sanders about a series of threatening voicemails on a Colorado football ticket office phone line that mentioned him. At the time, Sanders was just six months into the job and had yet to coach a game. "I guess this confirms what you are working on," Sanders told Evis McGee, a member of his personal security team, after learning about the voicemails, per the police report. DEION SANDERS SAYS ALLEGED $50,000 OFFER TO SILENCE CRITICS WAS 'A JOKE' AMID COLORADO'S STRUGGLES The voicemails proved not to be an isolated incident. The Athletic ultimately discovered 15 closed University of Colorado police cases involving harassment or suspicious activity directed at Sanders since he left Jackson State and was named the Buffaloes head coach. Two additional cases remain open, with records unavailable, and most stem from 2023. In a YouTube video posted in January by Sanders’ son, Deion Jr., Michael Rhodes warned players to "be mindful of who comes in [the facility] with you, especially on the elevator." Rhodes delivered those comments during an introductory meeting ahead of the 2026 season. "Don’t let somebody coerce you into scanning them up on the floor, because everybody’s trying to get to Coach Prime," he continued. Rhodes is the head of Sanders' university-paid security team. "Some people say, ‘Coach, what do you need a head of security for?’ We get death threats all the time," said Sanders. "Why? I’m a Black man making it happen. … That stuff is real. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "How many death threats we get?" Sanders was shown in the video asking Rhodes. He responded: "About five every day." MATT RHULE DRAWS THE LINE AFTER FAN VERBALLY ATTACKS HIS 13-YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER FOLLOWING LATEST NEBRASKA LOSS Colorado athletics said its security efforts involve Sanders’ personal security team as well as the CU Boulder Division of Public Safety. "The safety of Coach Prime is our top priority, and we take every threat seriously," the athletics department said in a statement. "CU Athletics works closely with the CU Boulder Division of Public Safety to coordinate security efforts with Coach Prime’s entire team, including his security detail, and respond appropriately to reported threats." Nearly half of the 15 closed cases The Athletic reviewed were found to have ties to one individual who repeatedly mailed threatening letters. The letters contained incoherent passages and biblical references, along with racist remarks directed at Sanders. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Colorado has two games remaining on its 2026 schedule and needs to win both to become bowl eligible, something that seemed completely out of reach earlier in the season. Sanders led the Buffaloes to a 42-32 upset of Houston last week.

articles.title: Watch Alex Ovechkin Make History on Video as NHL Legend Breaks Capitals Record
articles.summary: Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin is still making history a year and a half after breaking Wayne Gretzky's all-time goalscoring record.
articles.body:
Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin is still making history a year and a half after breaking Wayne Gretzky's all-time goalscoring record.

Ovechkin recorded his 763rd career helper Thursday night against the visiting Buffalo Sabres to pass former linemate Nicklas Bäckström for the Capitals' franchise lead in assists.

The play set up Boone Jenner for a goal that cut the Capitals' deficit to 5-3 in the final 10 minutes of the third period.

Bäckström played 17 seasons and won a Stanley Cup with the Capitals before he stepped away due to health reasons in 2023. He recorded 279 of his assists on goals from Ovechkin.

Ovechkin, whose 930 goals make him the most prolific scorer in NHL history, ranks second among active players with 1,693 points as well as sixth in assists. The 41-year-old announced in October he will be retiring after the 2026-27 season.

articles.title: Why is Zac Taylor so excited Paycor is hosting Elder-Princeton?
articles.summary: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said he's thrilled that Elder and Princeton are playing their high school playoff regional final game at Paycor Stadium.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said he's thrilled that Elder and Princeton are playing their high school playoff regional final game at Paycor Stadium on Friday.

"I love it," Taylor said. "I mean, I really do love it. I'll be following the game. We'll be working since our week's a little different. So I'll get to hear the environment out there and maybe poke my head out. But two programs that have had great years. I've watched them both over the course of the season."

"So it should be a great game," Taylor continued. "It's awesome that they're doing it here at Paycor. I think that's a really cool experience for those kids. (I) went to the game last year when it was St. X and Elder and watched a lot of high school football this year."

The Bengals take on the Steelers with a white out Sunday evening

"I'm not always at the games, but I'm certainly watching on streams and following on Twitter to see what the scores are," Taylor added. "And a lot of programs that I like to follow as I've gotten to know some coaches. So the Elder-Princeton game's going to be a great game."

The day after the Bengals' rout of Pittsburgh on " Sunday Night Football ," Taylor talked about how impressed he was with right tackle Amarius Mims' dominant effort against TJ Watt and the Steelers ' defense.

Taylor was asked after the game whether he heard MVP chants for Burrow from the crowd.

"Well, I mean, (it would) be impossible to say anybody's playing better than him," Taylor told reporters after the game. "I'm not watching every game, but I can promise you people that aren't talking about him aren't watching all of our games because if you are, it's really hard to say that this dude's not the best player on planet Earth."

articles.title: Mykhailo Mudryk, Ukraine national team play the blame game over failed doping test
articles.summary: He said; they said
articles.body:
Mykhailo Mudryk hasn't done anything of note on the pitch since returning to football this summer, but he did sit down in front of the microphone recently and put the Ukraine football federation and national team on blast, blaming them for his failed doping control back in 2024 .

Speaking on some podcast called "Guest of Gordon", Mudryk accused the national team setup for not having standards and handing out the pills that contained the banned — well, banned at the time — substance meldonium.

"It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England. "The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team. There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup." -Mykhailo Mudryk; source: Guest of Gordon via The Standard

"It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.

"The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team. There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup."

Mykhailo Mudryk; source: Guest of Gordon via The Standard

Mudryk had maintained his innocence from the very start and always claimed that he did not knowingly ingest any banned substance. While the specific concentration of meldonium that Mudryk had in his system is no longer considered a doping violation — thus the lifting of the ban last summer — he still lost nearly two years of his career, not to mention the hit to his reputation and professionalism. And if he blames the national team for the whole thing, that's certainly understandable given the the test was done while he was on national team duty.

Of course, athletes are always responsible for what they take at the end of the day — whether handed to them by a team doctor, a physio, or some random trainer or family friend — but there is a level of trust that is inherently expected in these situation as well, and that has been clearly broken for Mudryk.

Obviously, the Ukraine national team haven't taken well to this accusation, with their president firing back after Mudryk's quotes made the media rounds. Incidentally, the president is none other than Andriy Shevchenko, another player with a rather tumultuous time at Stamford Bridge.

"Loud statements have been made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally." "After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during national team training camps. The national team staff complied with this request. Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps. These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine." "[…] If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologize to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question." -Andriy Shevchenko; source: The Athletic

"Loud statements have been made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally."

"After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during national team training camps. The national team staff complied with this request. Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps. These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine."

"[…] If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologize to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question."

I don't imagine this is doing any good for Mudryk's national team career … though with just one substitute appearance so far this season to his name (thanks in part to an ankle injury), there isn't much of a career to speak of at the moment. If one of your biggest fans, Roberto De Zerbi isn't giving you the minutes, those you just insulted aren't going to be lining up at your door either.

The 25-year-old (still just 25!) is set to return from said ankle injury this weekend. Hopefully things start improving for him soon.

articles.title: Sabres beat Capitals 6-3, sending Washington to 4th straight loss
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Rasmus Dahlin and Beck Malenstyn scored 25 seconds apart in the first period to chase Logan Thompson, and the Buffalo Sabres sent Washingto...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Rasmus Dahlin and Beck Malenstyn scored 25 seconds apart in the first period to chase Logan Thompson, and the Buffalo Sabres sent Washington to its fourth straight loss, beating the Capitals 6-3 on Thursday night.

Jack Quinn scored twice — once into an empty net — and Zach Benson and Tage Thompson also scored for the Sabres. Buffalo converted on five of its 13 shots in the first two periods. Alex Tuch, Ryan Leonard and Boone Jenner scored Washington, which has fallen to .500 after entering the season with lofty expectations.

Alex Ovechkin broke a tie with longtime teammate Nicklas Backstrom for Washington's career lead in assists with his 763rd.

The Capitals have allowed at least five goals in four straight games and six of their last eight. On Wednesday it took them only two periods to do so. Thompson allowed three goals on five shots before being yanked in favor of Charlie Lindgren.

It was the second time in his last six starts Thompson was pulled early.

After Quinn opened the scoring, Dahlin entered the zone on a power play, and when Thompson overplayed him a bit to the near post, the Buffalo defenseman swooped behind the net and wrapped the puck into the vacated other side.

Malenstyn made it 3-0 and Thompson's night was done.

Tuch scored again against his former team. He had two goals against Buffalo, including the winner in overtime , in a game last month.

It was 4-1 after one Thursday, and Tage Thompson scored on the power play near the end of the second. Leonard scored to cap a dominant stretch on the power play for Washington in the third, then Jenner poked the puck in with 10:16 remaining after Buffalo goalie Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen seemed unaware it was loose.

Ovechkin received an assist on Jenner's goal, having passed to him in the neutral zone before Jenner dumped the puck toward the net, followed it and poked it in.

With neither team playing particularly well of late, Washington's Tom Wilson and Buffalo's Sam Carrick dropped the gloves right off the opening faceoff. Both were given fighting majors just one second into the game.

articles.title: Notre Dame stays hot with 78-73 win over Auburn in Players Era Tournament
articles.summary: Notre Dame officially finishes 5th in the Players Era Tournament in Las Vegas, but this all feels much bigger.
articles.body:
The Notre Dame Fighting Irish keep winning basketball games, and they closed out the Players Era 8 in Las Vegas with a 78-73 win over the Auburn Tigers. Braeden Smith continues to look like one of the great steals of the transfer portal, and there is real momentum now early in the season to find the Irish back in the AP Top 25.

Irish Take Down Auburn Tigers In 78-73 Victory

LAS VEGAS – The (RV) Notre Dame men's basketball team (6-1) took down the Auburn Tigers (3-3) in a 78-73 victory as the Irish completed a 2-1 week at the Players Era 8 and continue to be big early season movers in KenPom. The Irish were led yet again by veteran point guard, Braeden Smith, who finished the night with 23 points – now 53 points on the week in Vegas. He finished the night 7-of-11 from the floor and 8-for-9 from the free throw line, while grabbing 8 rebounds and dishing out 4 assists. Smith shot 17-for-22 over the last two games. He dished out 15 assists over the last three. Senior Braeden Shrewsberry also poured in 18 points on a 7-for-14 shooting night as he finished the week with 51 points at the Players Era 8. They were followed by sophomore Brady Koehler with 15 points and 8 boards, shooting 4-for-10 from floor and 3-of-5 from behind the arc. Koehler had himself a trip out west as he led all Irish players with 59 points on the week He averaged 7.0 rebounds per game over the three games and was 10-of-16 from three-point range. Fifth year Logan Duncomb also finished the night in double-digits as he finished with 10 points in the win, shooting 4-5 from the floor, while also contributing a pair of rebounds and three assists. The Irish finished the night shooting 25-for-51 at a clip of 49.0 percent, while going 8-31 (38.1 percent) from beyond the arc. Auburn finished with a 22-for-54 shooting performance (40.7 percent) from the floor and finished shooting 31.0 percent on 9-of-29 from three. It was a game of free throws, as the Irish and Tigers shot a combined 33 in the second half for a total of 55 on the night. The Irish finished the night 20-27 from the line and Tigers were there with them, going 20-28 from the charity stripe. Thus, over the last three games, the Irish averaged 88.7 ppg on 54.8 percent shooting from the floor. They averaged 9.7 threes per game on a 41.4 percent clip from beyond the arc. HOW IT HAPPENED Notre Dame's defense forced three turnovers in the opening minutes while four of the five starters contributed buckets, claiming a 14-8 lead The Irish had started 6-for-10 from the field, led by seven points from Braeden Smith. Auburn countered with a 9-0 scoring run spanning 2:12, capturing their first lead of the game, up 17-14. Next, Smith made it a 4-for-4 start from the field, while Shrewsberry connected on back-to-back buckets in the paint. At this point, the Irish were 9-of-18 from the floor, compared to the Tiger's 8-for-18, and trailed 26-23. Out of the under-eight media timeout, Logan Imes drained a corner three, which was followed immediately by and-one from Logan Duncomb. This sequence ultimately spurred a 16-2 Irish scoring run in which they made five straight from the field. Meanwhile, Auburn went 1-of-9 from the field during said stretch. The Tigers garnered some momentum late with a quick 6-0 run to cut it to one possession but it was answered by a Shrewsberry triple. The senior guard then tacked on two free throws with nine seconds remaining, while Notre Dame's defense earned a final stop, taking us to our halftime score of 42-36. The Irish shot 50.0 percent from the floor on 13-26 shooting, while holding Auburn to 12-30 shooting at a 40.0 percent clip. The ND offense also took care of the ball, only coughing up two turnovers. Auburn notched a 6-1 offensive board advantage, in which they converted into nine second-chance points. Shrewsberry led all players at halftime with 14 points on 5-9 shooting. He was followed by Smith with 13 points on a perfect 4-4 shooting performance, knocking down one triple and going 4-4 from the charity stripe. At the under-16 media, it was 51-44 Notre Dame. The Irish had sunk four straight heading into the break, while the Tigers stayed close with a pair of triples. Over the next four minutes, when Auburn cut it to one possession, Notre Dame answered with a score, getting contributions from both Shrewsberry and Imes. Yet, the Irish couldn't muster any breathing room either, up just 55-52 with 11:39 remaining. Auburn tied the game with a corner three out of the break. Down on the other end, Jonathan Sanderson punched back with a triple. It was back-and-forth scoring between the two squads as the Irish found answers from Koehler and Shrewsberry until it was tied up yet again at 65-all with 7:15 left. In fact, from 8:57 to the 3:57 media timeout, ND's lead never exceeded three points, which also included four ties. Koehler scored seven points during this span. Out of the timeout, the Irish sunk three free throws to extend their lead to five, but a finish at the rim from Auburn would make it a one-possession game yet again at 75-72 with 2:15 remaining. The Tigers went 2-8 from the charity stripe down the stretch, missing six consecutive free throws in the final four minutes of play. With the Irish up 75-73 with 15 seconds left, Smith was relentless in his efforts against the Tigers as his tough, crafty left-handed finish at the rim extended the Irish lead to four. Notre Dame followed with a steal from Koehler on the Tigers' inbounds pass with just under eight seconds remaining. Fouled on the steal, Koehler closed it out with one more free throw to secure the 78-73 win over Auburn. UP NEXT Plenty of opportunity awaits the Irish and it'll all be at home. That's right, Notre Dame will play nine straight inside Purcell Pavilion starting with Central Michigan on Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers in Favor of Notable Change at Steelers Practices
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers were flat-out embarrassed last Sunday night against the Cincinnati Bengals. The team was fresh off a bye week and looked like they di...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers were flat-out embarrassed last Sunday night against the Cincinnati Bengals. The team was fresh off a bye week and looked like they did not practice at all for the first-place showdown against the Bengals.

The final score of 38-18 hides just how awful the Steelers were, especially on offense.

Aaron Rodgers' unit could barely gain positive yardage throughout the first three quarters, while the defense was getting carved up by Joe Burrow all night.

The good news is the team is still 6-3 and appears to be a playoff lock in a weak AFC. Yet nothing is for certain after how bad the team looked in Cincinnati.

That is why veteran defender Cam Heyward suggested a change in how the team practices. Rodgers backed up his teammate on the idea.

Steelers Veterans Want Tougher Practices

Rodgers spoke with the media Thursday and mentioned how he agreed with Heyward on how the team needs more physicality at practice, per 93.7 The Fan on X . He also said he knows a few guys who may be willing to start a fight in practice to ramp up the intensity.

Jokes aside, this suggestion makes a lot of sense after how last Sunday went. The Steelers were fresh off a bye week and waited until Sunday night to take on the Bengals. The game itself made it seem like the Steelers didn't even practice all week.

This came after a dominant 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns back in Week 8 heading into the bye. That was the team's fourth win in a row and it seems all the momentum from that was ended with the week off.

The Steelers may not need to physically fight in practice, but getting more competitive will help avoid an upset loss this weekend against Joe Milton and the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles.

Pittsburgh Still in Comfortable Playoff Position

The Steelers enter the week in the sixth spot in the AFC standings. The Browns are in seventh at 6-4, followed by the New England Patriots at 5-5. Drake Maye's injury injury may take Mike Vrabel's team out of contention. Next up are the Las Vegas Raiders and Baltimore Ravens at 4-6, respectively.

Thus, Pittsburgh is in great shape with eight games remaining.

But a surprise loss to the Eagles could send things off the rails. That is why the veterans are locking in and making sure everyone takes this week of preparation seriously.

Fans will see Sunday if this was all talk or an effective message.

articles.title: White Sox rumors: What Chicago is planning after Luis Castillo salary dump

The Chicago White Sox made a trade with the Colorado Rockies on Thursday. Chicago dealt pitchers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin to Colorado for left-handed pitcher Sean Sullivan and catcher Douglas Veliz. For the White Sox, the deal represented an opportunity to move on from Castillo's $20 million salary. According to Bob Nightengale of USA Today, the White Sox are planning to bring in more starting pitching with additional money to spend now.

The White Sox already signed Dustin May to a $52.5 million contract . He seemingly is not going to be their only pitching acquisition this offseason. Chicago wants to bring in another starting pitcher or two.

Moving from Castillo and Martin won't help their current rotation outlook, but signing a starter such as Freddy Peralta or Michael King would obviously give them a boost.

Chicago acquired Castillo during the 2026 MLB season. He's a veteran pitcher who happens to be a three-time All-Star, but he pitched to a lackluster 8.42 ERA across nine outings with the White Sox after this past season's trade.

Martin, meanwhile, turned in a respectable 3.95 ERA in his 29 outings (28 starts) during the '26 campaign. Moving on from him was surely especially difficult, but it allowed the White Sox to move Castillo's lucrative deal. Now Chicago can focus on upgrading their rotation as the team hopes to take the next step in 2027.

The 2026 season saw the White Sox reach the postseason. They were eliminated in the American League Division Series by the Cleveland Guardians. Chicago would love to make a deeper postseason run next year.

articles.title: Five players David Ferrer could call upon to replace Carlos Alcaraz if he withdraws from Davis Cup Finals with injury

articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz could miss the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna.

After requiring treatment against Daniil Medvedev at the ATP Finals, Alcaraz underwent an MRI . He has been cleared to continue in Turin, but whether he will be fit to complete the tournament and then play the Davis Cup Finals next week remains to be seen.

Spain's Davis Cup captain, David Ferrer, said he needs Alcaraz to win the title , but what happens if they lose their star man? Here are five players Ferrer could call upon to replace him for the trip to Bologna.

Five players who could replace Carlos Alcaraz at the Davis Cup Finals

Spanish veteran Pablo Carreno Busta would be a solid replacement for Alcaraz. The 35-year-old won the Davis Cup with Spain back in 2019, and knows what it takes to be a member of a winning side.

His form isn't the best, having lost his last three matches, but assuming Rafael Jodar is promoted to the number one singles slot, Carreno Busta could still have a lot to give as a number two.

Jaume Munar was Spain's number one at last year's Davis Cup Finals when Alcaraz withdrew. He beat Jiri Lehecka before losing to Alexander Zverev and Flavio Cobolli, as his country fell to Italy in the final.

Munar played his last match of the season in Stockholm 11 days ago, before his first child was born earlier this week. Whether he is prepared to play for his country at the Davis Cup on short notice after such a major life event is for him and Ferrer to decide.

According to his social media, Martin Landaluce is already enjoying his off-season, travelling to Venice with his partner. Like Munar, the question is whether he could be pried away from his break to line up for Spain in Bologna.

Landaluce would be a great addition to the Spanish side, and he has already played his part in getting them to the Davis Cup Finals. Landaluce won his first Davis Cup match in September against Matias Soto, as Spain beat Chile 4-0 in the qualifier.

Munar and Landaluce may not be 100% ready, but Inaki Montes De La Torre certainly is. The 24-year-old isn't exactly a household name and has yet to make his Davis Cup debut, but he is playing and winning matches this week.

Montes De La Torre is through to the quarter-finals of the Challenger Tour event in Mertz, France, winning his first two matches in straight sets. In form and ready to go, the world number 189 could be an interesting left-field option for Ferrer.

Like Montes De La Torre, Daniel Rincon has been in action this week. The two-time Challenger Tour title winner finished a stint in South America with a defeat in the first round of the Montevideo Challenger.

If Ferrer wants a player who has been active this week, and will surely be eager to impress on his Davis Cup debut, Rincon might be the man to call.

The 2026 Davis Cup Finals begin on November 24. Spain will play Austria in the quarter-finals on November 26.

articles.title: Rick Neuheisel picks Washington to upset Indiana
articles.summary: A former Washington coach picked Jedd Fisch and the Huskies to upset Curt Cignetti and the No. 8 Indiana Hoosiers.
articles.body:
With just one game remaining at Husky Stadium in the 2026 season, Jedd Fisch's team is still looking for its first win against a Big Ten opponent at home, and on Senior Day, Washington will face its toughest conference foe, coach Curt Cignetti and the No. 8 Indiana Hoosiers .

Fisch lost his only matchup with Cignetti and the Hoosiers in Bloomington, 31-14 in 2024, but former UW coach Rick Neuheisel gave Washington's third-year head coach a vote of confidence and picked the Huskies to upset the Hoosiers.

"The numbers obviously tell us that it's going to be an Indiana day," Neuheisel said on CBS Sports. "I've been to Husky Stadium, and I know what happens when the 12th, 13th, 14th man get involved, and I think the Husky crowd will come out in number to watch this game, I think Demond Williams and that crew there wearing purple are going to get it done, it's my upset of the week."

One of the biggest keys to finding a way to pull off the upset will be limiting Indiana's standout pair of wide receivers, Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, who both rank inside the top ten in the Big Ten in receiving yards, and have been projected as first round picks in the 2027 NFL draft.

"We'll definitely have a plan," defensive coordinator Ryan Walters said on Tuesday. "It poses more difficult challenges because they play on opposite sides, so you kind of have to pick your poison, but we can't just play the way we always play. We definitely have to have some wrinkles to limit the explosive plays through the air."

With some struggles at quarterback despite the standout pair of pass catchers, the Hoosiers rank No. 7 in passing offense against Big Ten opponents, averaging 240.7 yards per game, and No. 8 against conference foes in scoring offense at 24.9 points per game.

They outscored Charleston by 14 points in the final half, as Carroll led the way with a team-high 17 second-half points.

articles.title: Report: Padres Meet With No. 1 Free Agent Tarik Skubal
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres reportedly hosted top free agent Tarik Skubal on Wednesday afternoon. The consensus No. 1 free agent on the market is almost certain to...
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres reportedly hosted top free agent Tarik Skubal on Wednesday afternoon. The consensus No. 1 free agent on the market is almost certain to break the record for the largest contract by a starting pitcher in MLB history. Skubal and his agent, Scott Boras, are reportedly starting the bidding at $325 million, which is the current record.

Whether San Diego's new owners have the ability to sign a player of Skubal's caliber while continuing to add to the roster is another reality of the situation. The Padres haven't increased payroll much since former owner Peter Seidler passed away. San Diego's new ownership have affirmed their desire to make a big splash this offseason. How might that affect their commitment to the Skubal sweepstakes?

Tarik Skubal is potentially the greatest living pitcher on the planet. That might seem overzealous, but he's got the numbers to back it up. Skubal has posted a sub-3.00 ERA in four consecutive seasons. In both seasons that he threw 160-plus innings, Skubal struck out more than 200 batters. He won back-to-back Cy Young Awards in 2024 and '25 and is one of the most dominant left-handers of the last few years.

Because of that, Skubal is believed to earn a contract worth upwards of $400 million. He's also projected to be signed to a deal of almost nine years. That would lock up the 29-year-old until his age-38 season. He almost certainly won't be as dominant as he is now for the entirety of that contract, but even four years of the ace is worth the hefty price tag.

San Diego has been listed as a long shot destination for Skubal. However, the club continues to pop up in rumors from league insiders. The Blue Jays and Mets are believed to be the frontrunners for Skubal. Their rotation needs are far less dire than San Diego's. Toronto has Dylan Cease as their ace (runner-up in 2026 AL Cy Young voting) and the Mets have Nolan McLean anchoring their rotation.

The Padres' needs go beyond just one dominant ace. That could hurt them. The club currently only has Randy Vásquez on the roster as a viable starting pitcher. Not even veteran Joe Musgrove is expected to begin the season in the rotation, as the righty continues to work back from Tommy John surgery. If the Padres do sign Skubal, that can't be the end of their free agency pursuits. San Diego needs a premier outfield bat along with several reliable starting pitchers .

That need suggests that the Padres might be better off not signing Skubal. Sure, the new owners want to make a splash, but that could be in signing two marquee starting pitchers instead of pooling all of their resources to sign one ace. Reuniting with Michael King and signing Freddy Peralta could be just as effective, if not more. It's unwise for San Diego to get into a bidding war with the Mets or Blue Jays unless they're willing to massively increase payroll for the foreseeable future.

The fit is obvious for the Padres. San Diego has lacked a perennial ace for quite some time. King has done his best to be that for the Friars in 2024 and '26, but hasn't maintained enough consistency. Instead, the Padres have taped together their rotation year after year. Skubal would immediately provide some consistency that could lengthen the Padres' contention window.

It's believed by many that Skubal will eventually sign with the Mets . That being said, he has expressed interest in remaining on the West Coast. Skubal was born in Hayward, California, and was later raised in Kingman, Arizona. It remains to be seen how much that could affect his decision, but any advantage helps. A.J. Preller has proven himself to be one of the most creative front office executives in baseball. If new ownership gives him the financial flexibility to sign Skubal, it's seems near certain that he'll take a chance on the ace.

articles.title: Hutson strikes twice late, including for the OT winner, as Canadiens beat Hurricanes 2-1
articles.summary: (AP) — Lane Hutson scored twice in the final 5-plus minutes, including the finish on a perfect give-and-go feed from Nick Suzuki in the first minute of overt...
articles.body:
RALEIGH, N.C. (AP) — Lane Hutson scored twice in the final 5-plus minutes, including the finish on a perfect give-and-go feed from Nick Suzuki in the first minute of overtime, to help the Montreal Canadiens rally past the Carolina Hurricanes 2-1 on Thursday night.

The reigning Stanley Cup champion Hurricanes led this rematch of last year's Eastern Conference Final coming down the stretch of the third period before Hutson struck.

First he came in the left side to bang the puck into the top left corner past Pyotr Kochetkov to tie it at 1-1 at the 15:01 mark of the third. Then he fed Suzuki on the right side and immediately skated toward the crease with a step on Carolina's Sebastian Aho. Suzuki's feed was on target, and Hutson waited out Kochetkov as the goaltender sprawled to the ice before lifting the puck over him and into the net.

Suzuki assisted on Hutson's first goal as well, while Jakub Dobes finished with 26 saves as Montreal followed Wednesday's 3-2 win at New Jersey for wins on back-to-back nights.

Nikolaj Ehlers scored for the Hurricanes, breaking a scoreless tie midway through the third period when he zipped a shot past Dobes into the top left corner. Kochetkov finished with 22 saves.

Carolina entered Thursday leading the league in points percentage (.810), ahead of Edmonton as the only other team at 80% or better in the standings. The Hurricanes had won four straight, which included sweeping a two-game set against Seattle in Finland last week by a combined 9-2 score.

The Hurricanes had won the first meeting 6-4 in Montreal's home opener in early October, pushing ahead for good midway through the second period. This one marked the Canadiens' first trip to Raleigh since a 6-1 loss on May 29 that closed out the Eastern final in five games.

Montreal played without forward Zachary Bolduc, who left the New Jersey win with an upper-body injury.

Canadiens: The Canadiens return home to face the Philadelphia Flyers on Saturday.

Hurricanes: The Hurricanes host the Edmonton Oilers on Saturday.

articles.title: Curt Cignetti Michigan Coaching Rumors
articles.summary: Indiana coach Curt Cignetti fired back at rumors linking him to Michigan's coaching job, calling the report fake news in a fiery social media post.
articles.body:
Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti has made it abundantly clear what he thinks about speculation linking him to the Michigan Wolverines. And judging by his response Thursday night, he isn't interested in entertaining the idea.

Following a November 19 report from CBS Sports that identified Cignetti as a potential candidate if Michigan moves on from head coach Kyle Whittingham, the Indiana coach took to social media to deliver a blunt response. He didn't mince words, and he even included a clown emoji for good measure.

"Fake news created by three SEC media writers. Nice try 🤡"

Cignetti posted the message on his official X account , directly challenging the report that had connected him to a possible opening in Ann Arbor.

Why Curt Cignetti Was Linked to Michigan

The speculation began with a November 19 CBS Sports report from John Talty, Richard Johnson, and Chris Hummer examining potential movement on the college football coaching carousel. With Whittingham's future at Michigan increasingly uncertain, Cignetti emerged as one of several prominent coaches who could theoretically enter the conversation.

The report suggested that Cignetti had concerns about Indiana's ability to sustain its success financially and replace departing talent ahead of the 2027 season. Those concerns reportedly raised questions about whether a program with Michigan's resources might appeal to the Indiana coach.

According to the CBS Sports report, sources suggested that Cignetti had discussed the possibility of significant roster turnover with members of his staff. However, the report did not establish that Michigan had formally contacted Cignetti or that negotiations were taking place.

Cignetti clearly wasn't impressed with the speculation, and his public response left little room for interpretation.

Michigan's Coaching Situation Continues to Generate Speculation

The rumors come as Michigan faces growing uncertainty following a disappointing 2026 season under Whittingham. The Wolverines are 5-5, and their embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State only intensified questions about the direction of the program.

Michigan has already made one significant coaching change, parting ways with offensive coordinator Jason Beck . The arrival of incoming athletic director Trev Alberts has also fueled discussion about whether Whittingham will return for a second season.

Earlier Thursday, CBS Sports identified five high-profile coaching possibilities if the Wolverines decide to make another change. Along with Cignetti, the names included UCLA's Bob Chesney, Alabama's Kalen DeBoer, Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, and Missouri's Eli Drinkwitz.

Still, Michigan has not announced a coaching vacancy, and Whittingham remains the Wolverines' head coach. The conversation surrounding potential replacements remains hypothetical unless the university decides to move in another direction.

Cignetti's reaction is particularly noteworthy considering what he has accomplished at Indiana. After leading the Hoosiers to a national championship following the 2025 season, he has continued to establish the program as a legitimate contender in the Big Ten.

Indiana enters the weekend with a 9-1 record, while Michigan continues searching for answers during a frustrating season. For Wolverines fans hoping to see Cignetti eventually arrive in Ann Arbor, Thursday's response certainly wasn't encouraging.

The Indianapolis Star also reported that a source familiar with the situation rejected the idea of Cignetti leaving Indiana for Michigan. That additional reporting reinforced the coach's public dismissal of the speculation.

Of course, college football coaching searches can produce unexpected developments, and Michigan's future remains unsettled. But based on Cignetti's own words, anyone hoping to see him leave Bloomington for Ann Arbor might want to start looking elsewhere.

One thing is certain: Curt Cignetti has no interest in letting this rumor go unanswered. And he just made the Michigan coaching conversation a little more interesting.

The Blue were on cruise control the rest of the way. They put up 23 points in the fourth quarter. They led by as many as 31 points. The entire active roster had the chance to log serious minutes.

The Blue shot 47% from the field and went 18-of-41 (43.9%) from 3. They shot 9-of-14 on free throws. They had 32 assists on 40 baskets. Five Blue players scored double-digit points.

articles.summary: WINNIPEG, Manitoba (AP) — Josh Morrissey scored his first goal of the season with 3:02 left in overtime to lift the Winnipeg Jets to a 4-3 victory over the N...
articles.body:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba (AP) — Josh Morrissey scored his first goal of the season with 3:02 left in overtime to lift the Winnipeg Jets to a 4-3 victory over the New York Islanders on Thursday night.

Kyle Connor scored his team-leading 18th goal and had an assist, and Morgan Barron and Cole Perfetti also scored for Winnipeg, which has won seven of eight. Mark Scheifele tallied three assists and Gabriel Vilardi added a pair.

Nico Daws made 22 saves to improve to 3-1 since being acquired from New Jersey in the Connor Hellebuyck deal .

Anthony Duclair, Emil Heineman and Kyle Palmieri scored for New York, which snapped its season-best win streak at three games. Semyon Varlamov stopped 18 shots.

After spending much of the overtime period in Winnipeg's end, Morrissey took a pass from Scheifele and fired a low shot past Varlamov.

Winnipeg went 1 for 2 on the power play. New York went 0 for 3 with the man advantage but got a short-handed goal from Heineman.

New York had three one-goal leads and never trailed until Morrissey ended it. Islanders star defenseman Matthew Schaefer snapped a six-game point streak.

The Islanders scored twice off egregious giveaways by the Jets. The first was from Daws, who tried to backhand a pass to the middle of the ice only to get snuffed out by Heineman. Then, early in the second period, Dylan Samberg coughed up a puck that led to Palmieri's goal.

articles.body:
Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit called Thursday's game between the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans . Late in the first half the Colts' kicker Spender Shrader lined up to attempt a 62-yard field goal. That kick was blocked by Texans' defensive lineman Logan Hall. Michaels was not impressed.

While blocked kicks are rare in the NFL, Michaels didn't even react. There was a loud thud as the ball hit Hall's hand and then Michaels flatly made his call. "So the kick is on the way and… blocked." Fans noticed the uninspiring tone in his voice because, honestly, it was hard to ignore. There wasn't even the slightest hint of excitement that fans had just seen something that was even mildly interesting.

It was not the first call on Thursday night that had people noting Michaels was either disinterested or having trouble keeping up with the action on the field. When A.J. Haulcy came away with a wild interception on a ball that bounced off his head, off a teammate and then back into his hands for an interception Michaels just sort of trailed off before proclaiming it may have been picked as the Colts ran towards the end zone to celebrate.
